The Bay Theatre in Pacific Palisades, which was formerly operated by Netflix and before that by Cinepolis, will be taken over by Paramount Pictures with San Diego’s The Lot handling operations. The opening is planned for later this year. The Bay Theatre has been closed since the wildfires damaged much of the upscale Los Angeles community in January 2025. The five-screen multiplex is located in Rick Caruso’s Palisades Village shopping area, which reopened in August after extensive remediation and repairs due to the fires. The theater’s vintage-looking sign is a nod to the community’s historic Bay Theatre, which stood nearby on Sunset Boulevard until closing in 1978. title: Fox Entertainment, Kevin Hart’s Hartbeat Sign Vertical Drama Deal
full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All October 13, 2026 9:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Kevin Hart Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images Fox Entertainment and Kevin Hart ‘s Hartbeat have struck a partnership that will see Fox tap Hartbeat’s original vertical series output as a development pipeline for future film and television projects. Under the agreement, announced at MIPCOM on Tuesday, Fox Entertainment Studios will have first-look rights for vertical series released under Hartbeat’s Codeblack, Essence and Revolt labels to develop the short-form series into feature and TV projects. Fox Entertainment Global will also distribute the original vertical series worldwide after each title’s initial platform run. Fox said the vertical dramas will be used to test stories and characters with audiences before committing to longer formats, including feature films and full-length TV series. “This partnership gives us an opportunity to identify bold ideas in the vertical space, see what resonates in real time, and give those stories a path to grow into film and television,” said Hannah Pillemer, head of scripted at Fox Entertainment Studios. “The culture builds the audience, the audience chooses the stories, and with Fox the stories that win become film and television for the world,” said Jeff Clanagan, founder of Codeblack and president and chief distribution officer of Hartbeat. full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Steve Stark’s Toluca Pictures Extends MGM TV Overall Deal, Expands Amazon MGM Studios First-Look Pact & Taps Max Kisbye As President ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ EP On How Harry Shum Jr. Juggles Medical Drama & ‘Dancing With The Stars’ & If It Affects His Presence On ABC Show ‘High Potential’ Gets Post-Super Bowl Slot, Eyes ‘Grey’s Anatomy’-Style 2-Parter On ABC & Disney+ View All October 13, 2026 9:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Steve Stark and Max Kisbye Gene Reed/Courtesy EXCLUSIVE : Steve Stark has extended and expanded his relationship with Amazon MGM Studios and its MGM Television division. His production company Toluca Pictures has signed a multi-year extension of its exclusive overall deal with MGM Television. Once again, it will include a first-look deal with Amazon MGM Studios, which is now being expanded beyond scripted TV to also include feature films and documentaries. Former MGM Television President Stark has named longtime MGM television executive Max Kisbye as President of Television & Film at Toluca Pictures. Kisbye succeeds Stacey Levin who recently left the company. Related Stories News 'Project Hail Mary' DoP Greig Fraser Says The Film Was The "Most Complicated" He's Ever Shot - Contenders London News 'Stargate' Series From 'WandaVision' Creator Jac Schaeffer In Works At Amazon Kisbye will work with Stark overseeing Toluca Pictures’ development and production operations. Additionally, the company has promoted longtime development executives Jessica Farrelly and Elan Fingles, along with creative executive Mia Stelling. Watch on Deadline “I am thrilled to have Max joining Toluca Pictures,” Stark said. “He is an exceptional executive with tremendous creative instincts, a go-getter with an incredible understanding of the business and, most importantly, a friend with a real passion for great storytelling. We have an incredibly ambitious slate ahead of us, and I couldn’t be more excited to have him alongside me. I’m equally excited to be expanding the roles of Jessica, Elan and Mia, who have been such an important part of building Toluca.” Stark and Kisbye have been friends for more than 20 years. Kisbye was a TV lit agent at CAA when Stark, then President of MGM Television TV, hired him as VP of Television Production in 2012. Kisbye most recently served as Senior Manager of Creative Development in MGM’s TV Scripted group. “I’ve always admired Steve’s instincts and his fearlessness in following them—whether that leads to a historical epic, a dark comedy, a documentary or something no one expects,” Kisbye said. “That spirit is what makes Toluca so exciting to me.” Stark launched Toluca Pictures in 2021 with a five-year overall deal at MGM Television after a nine-year stint as president of the TV studio. Toluca’s current slate includes flagship Netflix series Wednesday , which recently wrapped principal photography on its third season. The company also has coming up Nordic historical epic Bloodaxe , which is slated to premiere in January on Prime Video, as well as Mexican superhero series El Gato Negro, also for Prime Video. The company is in production on the second season of Hulu’s The Testaments and is set to begin production in 2027 on Fear Not , a true-story thriller starring Anne Hathaway for Paramount+. “Steve and I have been creative partners for years, and what he’s built at Toluca is a testament to his extraordinary taste and drive to make great content,” said Lindsay Sloane, Head of MGM Television. “From Wednesday to Bloodaxe to The Testaments , the range and ambition of what Toluca delivers is remarkable. And having worked closely with Max, I’ve seen his talent and passion firsthand.” Stark was under a producing deal with Universal Television in 2011 when he was recruited by Gary Barber, Roger Birnbaum and Roma Khanna to relaunch MGM Television following the studio’s 2010 bankruptcy. Some of the series he launched during his tenure building up the division include The Handmaid’s Tale for Hulu, Fargo for FX, and Vikings for History. Since he launched Toluca in 2021, the company has also produced the series The Consultant , starring Oscar winner Christoph Waltz for Amazon Prime Video, Vikings: Valhalla for Netflix, and The Bombing of Pan Am 103 , which recently premiered on Netflix and BBC, as well as the documentary The Devil’s Confession: The Lost Eichmann Tapes. “I’m incredibly grateful to Lindsay Sloane and my friends and colleagues at MGM Television, who have been extraordinary partners throughout this journey,” Stark said. “I’m also thankful for the continued support of Mike Hopkins, Peter Friedlander, and Kara Smith at Amazon MGM Studios.” Stark is repped by CAA and attorney Greg Slewett at JSSK. Kisbye is repped by David Matlof of Hirsch, Wallerstien, Hayum, Matlof and Fishman. title: From Haunted Morgues to Horror Movie Cabins, Airbnb’s Spookiest Stays Are Drawing Gen Z Travelers This Halloween
full_text: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission. Halloween is falling on a Saturday this year, and Gen Z is apparently looking to make a weekend of it. According to new data from Airbnb , searches for Halloween weekend stays have jumped nearly 45% among Gen Z travelers compared to last year, as younger vacationers look for more elaborate — and occasionally haunted — getaways. Overall searches for the Oct. 30-Nov. 1 weekend are up nearly 15% year-over-year, while wishlists with Halloween-inspired titles have increased almost 60%. Salem, Mass., perhaps unsurprisingly, ranks as the most popular trending U.S. destination for the holiday. Related Stories ‘Sin Filtro’ Producer JK Media Producing First Original Microdramas Shot in the U.S. for TelevisaUnivision’s ViXMicrO (EXCLUSIVE) Telly Awards Adds Microseries Competition Track, With Dozens of New Categories (EXCLUSIVE) To capitalize on the interest, Airbnb has rounded up 31 properties designed for different Halloween sensibilities, from cozy New England retreats that could double as the setting of “Gilmore Girls” to secluded horror-themed cabins and historic homes with reported paranormal activity. Some lean into the season with elaborate movie-inspired sets and interactive mysteries; others have histories that are unsettling enough on their own. Among the more unusual options is a former Missouri morgue equipped with ghost-hunting gear, a Nevada mining cabin previously featured on a paranormal reality series and a Big Bear retreat that borrows a particularly memorable bathroom scene from a horror classic. Here are seven stays worth considering for a Halloween weekend away — or a spooky getaway any time of year. BIG BEAR LAKE, CALIFORNIA Horror-Themed Cabin! Retro & Scary Movie Inspired For horror fans who would rather spend Halloween inside a scary movie than watching one, this Big Bear cabin goes all in on the genre. The retro-inspired rental features an elaborate bathroom modeled after a famous horror movie scene, complete with an axe lodged in the door. Ghostly special effects and an interactive escape-room mystery add to the atmosphere, making this one of the more theatrical options on Airbnb’s list. It’s an especially fitting getaway for fans planning a marathon of classic slasher films. BOOK Now OZARK, MISSOURI Historic Morgue and Paranormal Investigation! This Missouri property doesn’t have to manufacture much of its Halloween atmosphere. The building previously served as a morgue, funeral home, church and museum, and its current owners have leaned into that unusual history with mortuary-inspired decor. Guests staying in the loft can also try their hand at paranormal investigation with an included spirit box, electromagnetic field detector and dowsing rods. Whether any ghosts actually turn up is another question, but it’s a considerably more immersive alternative to watching an episode of “Ghost Hunters.” BOOK Now PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA The Hewitt For travelers whose Halloween tastes skew more gothic mystery than slasher film, Philadelphia’s Hewitt offers a suitably dramatic setting. Occupying the 2,500-square-foot third floor of an 1886 Queen Anne Victorian mansion in historic Germantown, the rental comes with period architecture and a hidden east wing accessible through a bookcase door. The setting lends itself to a weekend of murder mysteries, candlelit dinners and Victorian-era intrigue — without any actual haunting required. BOOK Now GREAT BARRINGTON, MASSACHUSETTS Berkshires Black Abbey A former church built in 1862 has been transformed into one of the more unusual group getaways in the Berkshires. The 4,000-square-foot property underwent a four-year conversion while retaining its original stained-glass windows and much of its ecclesiastical character. Modern additions include a cedar sauna and a game loft with a speakeasy-style bar. It’s an appealing option for groups looking to combine a foliage-filled New England weekend with something a little more gothic. BOOK Now BEATTY, NEVADA Haunted Mining Cabin Located roughly eight miles from the entrance to Death Valley National Park, this remodeled miner’s cabin dates back to the early 1900s and comes with a supernatural reputation. The property was previously featured on a paranormal reality series, though its reported haunting remains a matter of local lore rather than established fact. Its remote desert setting and mining history should appeal to travelers looking for something closer to a real-life ghost story than a conventional vacation rental. BOOK Now EAGLE HARBOR TOWNSHIP, MICHIGAN Anam Cara Cabin Not every Halloween getaway requires a ghost. Tucked away at the end of a winding gravel road in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula, Anam Cara Cabin is constructed from stone, timber and bark, with handmade lighting, a wood-burning fireplace and half a mile of shoreline. The remote lakeside property is especially suited to travelers interested in the quieter side of spooky season: dark skies, dense woods and the kind of solitude that would make a horror movie protagonist nervous. BOOK Now EXETER, NEW HAMPSHIRE The Word Barn For those who prefer the cozy side of fall, The Word Barn offers a more low-key New England escape. Located in a renovated farm barn in Exeter, New Hampshire, the apartment sits beside a literary and live-music venue in the countryside. Rather than haunted corridors or staged scares, the appeal here is autumn scenery and a weekend organized around books and performances. Cr. Andrew Levy/Netflix © 2026 Fresh off of his memoir Roll The Calls hitting The New York Times best seller list, WME executive chairman and TKO CEO Ari Emanuel is returning to his podcast. Emanuel and co-host Ben Persky will bring back their Rushmore podcast Oct. 20, seeing the pair team up with high-profile guests to debate the greatest people, events, and teams of all time. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell will be the guest on the season two premiere, debating the Mount Rushmore of NFL comebacks. Future episodes will include appearances from Pat McAfee (who is also a producer on the show), Shaquille O’Neal, Kevin Durant, Larry David, and Jerry Seinfeld. Season two is presented in partnership with nativ.ly and produced by Pantheon Media Group, filmed primarily in WME’s Beverly Hills headquarters. Episodes will be available on YouTube and other podcast platforms. “Everyone has their own Rushmore , and everyone thinks theirs is right,” said Emanuel. “Season Two turns up the volume with bigger debates, bigger personalities and even more people willing to tell us why we’re wrong.” “The debate is what gets us started, but the fun is in the stories and history that paint the conversation,” added Persky. “When you dig into what makes people the greatest, with the foremost experts of those fields, you get world-class perspective about the things we all obsess over.” Rushmore debuted last year , with guests that included Tom Brady, Elon Musk, Peyton Manning, Jeff Koons and Doris Kearns Goodwin, among others. “Ben and I have been on multiple vacations together, and we get into these conversations about the Mount Rushmore of all different topics,” Emanuel told THR last year of the show’s origins. “Finally, after a little bit, I said to him, we need to talk to an expert and get his point of view, because he thought my point of view was horrible and I thought his point of view was horrible.” Emanuel added, “It was just a conversation, and we picked subject matters that we were interested in at the time and that we thought we had really great people that were experts to engage with, and they did, and that’s what we wanted to do, and then it just kept on snowballing.” THR

title: Taiwan Gets Its Own Spotlight at Lumière, Led by Restored ‘Osmanthus Alley’ in Its Original Language
full_text: Oct 13, 2026 9:12am PT Taiwan Gets Its Own Spotlight at Lumière, Led by Restored ‘Osmanthus Alley’ in Its Original Language By Lin Ying-Hsuan Plus Icon Lin Ying-Hsuan Latest AI-Native Studios Can Create Original IP While Traditional Studios Keep Their Edge, VFX Veteran Hong Jae Cheol Says at Busan 2 days ago ‘Squid Game’ Producer Reads Founding Declaration as Asian Independent Producers Form Cross-Border Alliance at Busan 2 days ago Taiwan’s Sole Busan Competition Title ‘To Be Ordinary’ Marks Lee Yun Chan’s Return to Features After Two Decades 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Image Courtesy of NFAI Taiwan is getting a dedicated national focus at the International Classic Film Market ( MIFC ), the industry arm of Lyon’s Lumière Festival, the first for a non-European country, according to the Taiwan Film and Audiovisual Institute (TFAI). A new 4K restoration of Chen Kun-hou’s “ Osmanthus Alley ” leads the Taiwan in Focus program, which runs alongside this year’s guest country, Greece. Related Stories Raindance to Launch U.K.'s First Major Vertical Festival and Market (EXCLUSIVE) WWE Enters Microdrama Space With 'Agent of Shadows,' Drew McIntyre Takes Central Role TFAI is using the showcase to seek international distribution and programming partners for the island’s restored classics. “Osmanthus Alley” made its world premiere at the festival on Oct. 12, with Chen and star Lu Hsiao-fen in attendance. TFAI says distributors it has previously worked with have expressed interest, with release terms and timing still under negotiation. Adapted from Hsiao Li-hung’s novel, the film follows Thik-hông (Lu), an orphan who marries into a wealthy family, is widowed young and sees her son sent away to Japan, leaving her isolated behind the walls of the family estate. Simon Yam and Tuo Tsung-hua appear in guest roles. Lu won best actress at the 1987 Asia Pacific Film Festival, and the theme song, with lyrics by Wu Nien-jen, took the Golden Horse for best original film song. Popular on Variety The restoration also brings back the film’s original Taiwanese soundtrack. Chen insisted on shooting in Taiwanese, but state-run Central Motion Picture Corporation (CMPC) chose to release the film in Mandarin, in line with the government’s policy of promoting the language at the time. Chen eventually persuaded the studio to produce a Taiwanese version, but it played in only a limited number of theaters and gradually faded from view. Its selection coincides with the 70th anniversary of Taiwanese-language cinema, which TFAI traces to 1956’s “Xue Pinggui yu Wang Baochuan.” An estimated 1,200 Taiwanese-language films were made between the 1960s and 1981, but only about 200 survive in TFAI’s collection. The restoration also anticipates TFAI’s 2027 focus on literary adaptations, while Chen’s lifetime achievement award at the 2023 Golden Horse Awards prompted renewed interest in his work. Chen began as a cinematographer, winning a Golden Horse for “He Never Gives Up” (1978), and from 1979 worked closely with Hou Hsiao-hsien, the pair often trading roles behind the camera. Chen’s “Growing Up” won him the Golden Horse for best director in 1983. TFAI restored “Osmanthus Alley” from its original 35mm negative, filling missing frames from an interpositive, with audio drawn from the 35mm Taiwanese sound negative. The source was generally in good condition, but mold spots and dense clusters of small white specks required careful treatment. Aggressive cleaning settings risked erasing image detail, so technicians used masks and adjusted processing settings before completing frame-by-frame manual repairs. In line with FIAF’s code of ethics, Chen was repeatedly consulted. An intermediate version had more saturated, vibrant colors, but discussions with the director led to a more subdued final grade, closer to the original photography. Tu Duu-chih, who handled the film’s original sound mix, returned to help restore the Taiwanese soundtrack from six primary audio reels. The team synchronized the material, repaired damaged sections and reduced noise through multiple passes using light processing settings. The soundtrack holds another connection to Taiwanese cinema history. Cast members who did not speak Taiwanese were dubbed in post-production: co-star Lin Hsiu-ling voiced Lu’s dialogue, while Hou provided the voice for Tuo. TFAI, which holds about 20,000 film titles, restores 10 to 12 films a year and has restored more than 100 since 2013. Physical deterioration prompts climate control and emergency digitization, but a full restoration depends on whether a film has “a clear purpose and an audience ready to experience it right now,” the institute says. Recent restorations include Tsai Ming-liang’s “Vive L’Amour,” which screened in Venice Classics in 2025, and “The Dull Ice Flower,” chosen by Taiwanese audiences in a public poll and selected for Cannes Classics this year. Taiwanese-language titles “Love Never Ceases” and “Zhang Di Seeks A-Zu” were restored for the anniversary. Overseas, TFAI prioritizes in-person screenings to introduce lesser-known titles before pursuing distribution and streaming partnerships. “We want audiences to discover Taiwan cinema beyond Taiwan New Cinema and see the many different facets of Taiwan,” TFAI tells Variety . TFAI will also pitch its ongoing restoration of Yao Feng-pan’s “All in the Dim Cold Night” (1974) at MIFC’s Re>birth program on Oct. 15, seeking distributors and festival slots for the horror film. Often called Taiwan’s “King of Horror,” Yao built the film’s eerie atmosphere without modern visual effects, relying on practical techniques such as low-angle green lighting and burning straw on location. Taiwan in Focus also includes a round table with TFAI chair Arthur Chu and programmer Howard Yang, a networking event and an exhibition of original Taiwanese film posters. The institute hopes to build longer-term programming partnerships with international archives, giving restored Taiwanese films a life beyond their festival premieres. title: Ryan Coogler’s ‘X-Files’ Update Scores Hulu Series Order
full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All October 13, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Danielle Deadwyler, Himesh Patel and Ryan Coogler Melissa Alexander; Courtesy of Subject; Arturo Holmes/Getty Images Logo text The truth is still out there. A reboot of The X-Files shepherded by Ryan Coogler has landed a series order at Hulu . The Sinners filmmaker has been developing the project for several years , and he wrote and directed the pilot episode. Coogler will be an executive producer on the series, with Jennifer Yale ( Underground, See ) serving as showrunner. Onyx Collective and 20th Television produce along with Coogler’s Proximity Media. Danielle Deadwyler ( Rooster, The Harder They Fall ) and Himesh Patel ( The Odyssey ) will star in the series as “two highly decorated but vastly different FBI agents who form an unlikely bond when they are assigned to a long-shuttered division devoted to cases involving unexplained phenomena,” per the show’s logline. Related Stories TV 'All's Fair' Season 2 Is Back With a Vengeance -- and a Release Date TV Jamie Foxx Does Not Want to Be Canceled Over New Hulu Stand-up Special: "After That Kevin Hart Roast, I Had to Cut Everything" “I’ve loved The X-Files for a long time, so getting the chance to write and direct the pilot has meant a great deal to me,” said Coogler. “What Chris Carter created is special, and we wanted to honor everything that made the original series connect with so many people while also finding our own way into that world. Danielle and Himesh, along with the rest of our cast, have brought such original perspectives and performances to these characters, and watching that come together has been one of the most rewarding parts of the experience. I couldn’t have asked for better collaborators than my crew, colleagues at Proximity Media and our partners at Onyx Collective and 20th Television. I’m grateful for the trust and support they’ve given us as we take on this new chapter.” Created by Carter, The X-Files originally ran from 1993-2002 on Fox and spawned two feature films. Gillian Anderson and David Duchovny starred for most of the original run and in the two movies; Robert Patrick and Annabeth Gish starred in the latter stages of the show. Fox revived the show for two more seasons in 2016 and 2018, with Anderson and Duchovny returning to their roles as agents Dana Scully and Fox Mulder. Carter is an executive producer on the Hulu series alongside Coogler, Yale and Proximity Media’s Zinzi Coogler and Sev Ohanian. Deadwyler, Patel and Proximity’s Simone Harris are co-EPs. “We’re looking forward to continuing this journey as executive producers and especially excited to work closely with Jennifer Yale, Simone Harris, and the entire cast and crew as we bring this new chapter of The X-Files to life,” said Zinzi Coogler, Ohanian and Ryan Coogler in a statement. “It was also incredibly special to have our fellow Proximity co-founder Ludwig Göransson contribute the score for the pilot, making this a true collaboration across the Proximity family.” THR

title: Kim Kardashian Endorses On-Demand Apparel Delivery With New Skims x DoorDash Partnership and Ad Spot
full_text: × Skip to main content By Stacia Datskovska Plus Icon Stacia Datskovska View All October 13, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Daniel Sachon, Doordash, Skims If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission. It’s a tired industry trope: Missing that one essential item on set and failing to acquire it fast enough, no matter how many PAs are tapped for the task. And it turns out that Kim Kardashian is all too familiar with this pain point — so much so that she’s partnering with DoorDash to make her $5 billion apparel company, Skims , available for on-demand delivery via a platform that, in the past, strictly operated in the realm of food. As of Oct. 13 at 9 a.m. PT/12 p.m. ET, shoppers in more than 10 states can get almost-instant access to 29 Skims stores without ever stepping out of the house, as the purchases will be delivered straight to their door in as little as under an hour (delivery times may vary, according to DoorDash ). Related Stories Lifestyle 30 of the Most Fool-Proof (and Romantic) Anniversary Gifts for Him Lifestyle Nostalgia Fuels Halloween Decor Trends as Retailers Tap Into the 'Practical Magic' Aesthetic SKIP THE DELIVERY FEES WITH DASHPASS In that, Skims joins retailers like Urban Outfitters, The North Face, Gap and Anthropologie , which are already shoppable on DoorDash’s website and app under the “Retail” category, having become part of a growing trend that’s subjecting traditional retail to a kind of “quick commerce,” grocery- style treatment. Thanks to a limited-time promotion from DoorDash and Skims, users can also save 15 percent on Skims orders of $125 or more (up to $25 off) with promo code SKIMS15 at checkout. ”[The partnership] was inspired by conversations I had with my friends and family members, who think that I am Skims customer service. They call me all the time asking for a bodysuit , underwear or bra , and they need it now . They assume that I have a warehouse on speed dial,” Kardashian tells The Hollywood Reporter . “Out of my frustration, I thought, ‘How easy would it be if we were just connected to an app that, in a few taps, could get you the product, typically within an hour?'” View this post on Instagram The solution manifested quicker than expected: “Well, that’s DoorDash, actually,” Kardashian continues. “[I realized] this would be such a genius idea, so we made it happen. Now, if someone is demanding something from me, I just say, ‘Go to DoorDash. Leave me alone.'” DoorDash is Skims’ first-ever on-demand delivery partner, effectively revolutionizing the way devotees of the brand are able to get their hands on nonnegotiable, everyday staples (think Seamless Sculpt Brief Bodysuit ) and internet-viral, seasonal drops, like the label’s knitwear-forward Alpine Collection release . shop skims’ new alpine collection Eleventh-hour fashion emergencies happen — from not packing that one pair of compression shorts to realizing you have nothing to wear on the third date, despite an overflowing closet — and Skims is, famously, a problem solver by nature. “ My friends are all going to a wedding this weekend, and one of them was like, ‘Oh my gosh, I totally forgot to pack [a certain Skims piece] and I can’t get to the store in time.’ DoorDash is the most convenient thing for that,” Kardashian shares. The 45-year-old reveals another complication she has experienced in her professional life that could’ve easily been avoided with the Skims x DoorDash linkup : “ I was in a fitting, and there was a dress that was really tight, to the point of it flattening my chest. I needed a fuller bra that had padding in it to expand the dress, but I didn’t have it with me because I wasn’t at my house.” Daniel Sachon Besides bras, Skims’ core shapewear line is also something she envisions selling with success on DoorDash. shop skims’ shapewear “I wear shapewear under my dresses so that they’re not sheer. If you have a dress and you find out, right before going out, that it’s maybe a little bit more sheer than you imagined, this could be the quickest fix,” Kardashian offers. Customers can shop over 23,000 SKUs across Skims’ portfolio through DoorDash, and buying them there proves as simple and intuitive as ordering Chef Kim’s Magic Mineral Broth from Goop Kitchen when you’re sick. Skims’ unexpected landing at DoorDash was announced through a campaign directed by Daniel Sachon, produced by branded content studio OBB Bolded and shot at OBB Studios in Hollywood. In the ad spot, Kardashian can be seen urgently shopping for Skims push-up bras , nipple bras and other pieces on the DoorDash app: spotting elements of her look that need to be tweaked amidst an already high-stress photoshoot. She’s in pursuit of the perfect shot, after all, and, after a few deliveries, she nails it. “DoorDash was built on one idea: You should be able to get everything you need in your neighborhood, right now. And increasingly, that’s not just dinner, it’s what you’re wearing to dinner too,” Shanna Prevé, chief revenue officer at DoorDash, says in a press release. Whether it’s a sculpting savior that you plan on layering under your favorite denim or the Signature Swim Cut Out One Piece that’s going to save the day when none of your swimsuits fit the vibe for the bachelorette weekend (and airport check-in is in three hours), stocking up on Skims has never been more effortless. Forget what the psychologists told you: Instant gratification is highly encouraged. title: ‘14th’ Leads Critics Choice Documentary Awards Nominations
full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All October 13, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ava DuVernay with sitting Librarian of Congress Carla Hayden while making '14th.' Paul Garnes/Netflix Just days after making its world premiere at the New York Film Festival, Ava DuVernay’s 14th has landed the most nominations at the 2026 Critics Choice Documentary Awards . The Netflix film about the significance of and ongoing challenges to the 14th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution is nominated for best documentary feature, best director (DuVernay), best editing (Spencer Averick), best score (Jason Moran), best political documentary and best historical documentary. A number of documentaries landed the second-most nominations this year, with five nods apiece. The buzzy Elizabeth Holmes doc You Can See Everything , directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, is up for five awards, as are Once Upon a Time in Harlem and Nuisance Bear . Related Stories Movies Why 'Social Reckoning' Went Silent as More Tech Movies Face Box Office Test Movies Gaza Doc 'NAZA' Surpasses $500K Without Distributor After Sparking Protests Four-time nominees are Everybody to Kenmure Street, Remake , John Wilson’s The History of Concrete , Everest: The Other Side , EPIC: Elvis Presley in Concert , Lion and Rehearsals for a Revolution . Alex Gibney’s four-hour Elon Musk examination , Musk , and controversial Israel-Gaza war doc, NAZA , each landed three nods. The best documentary feature nominees are 14th, Everest: The Other Side, Everybody to Kenmure Street, The History of Concrete, Musk , NAZA , Once Upon a Time in Harlem, Rehearsals for a Revolution, Remake and You Can See Everything . “This year’s nominees reflect the range of voices, perspectives and stories that make documentary filmmaking so compelling,” The Critics Choice Association’s vp, documentary, Christopher Campbell, said in a statement. “These films challenge us to see the world in new ways and reinforce the vital role documentaries play in informing, engaging and inspiring audiences. We are proud to recognize the exceptional talent and creativity behind this year’s nominated films.” It was previously announced that Ron Howard would receive the Critics Choice Impact Award and Jehane Noujaim will receive lifetime achievement honor the Pennebaker Award. title: Peacock App Launches ‘Your Bravoverse,’ Featuring a Personalized TikTok-Style Video Feed Hosted by AI-Generated Andy Cohen
full_text: Oct 13, 2026 9:00am PT Peacock App Launches ‘Your Bravoverse,’ Featuring a Personalized TikTok-Style Video Feed Hosted by AI-Generated Andy Cohen By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Peacock App Launches ‘Your Bravoverse,’ Featuring a Personalized TikTok-Style Video Feed Hosted by AI-Generated Andy Cohen 28 minutes ago Hillary Clinton to Co-Host Podcast on 2026 Midterm Elections With Kara Swisher for Vox Media, Owned by James Murdoch 2 hours ago Ex-HBO Max and Legendary Execs Launch Twin Pines Entertainment, Studio Focused on Pro-Sports Movies and Series for America’s ‘Overlooked’ Heartland 2 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of NBCUniversal NBCUniversal ‘s Peacock is rolling out up a new way to try to get Bravo fanatics even more engaged in the network’s galaxy of reality programming drama and dish-worthy moments. On Tuesday, Peacock is bowing “Your Bravoverse,” a personalized stream of clips from Bravo shows, inspired by apps like TikTok, brought to you by a chatty AI avatar of Andy Cohen. NBCU announced the Your Bravoverse feature in the spring, as part of its broader road map for the Peacock app, and began testing it over the summer. Related Stories WWE Enters Microdrama Space With 'Agent of Shadows,' Drew McIntyre Takes Central Role Telly Awards Adds Microseries Competition Track, With Dozens of New Categories (EXCLUSIVE) Your Bravoverse, available now in the Peacock mobile app for all subscribers, serves up a “personalized feed of Bravo moments tailored to each fan,” including classic one-liners, meme-able moments and shocking reveals. An AI-generated avatar of Cohen, host of Bravo’s “Watch What Happens Live,” guides users through the experience with insider commentary. Popular on Variety “Bravo fans never watch just one episode,” Cohen said in a statement. “They want the backstory, the receipts and what happened three seasons later. Your Bravoverse on Peacock is built for exactly that! It’s a new way to go down every Bravo rabbit hole, rediscover iconic moments and find new ones based on what you love.” The Your Bravoverse personalized playlist of swipeable video clips is automatically built from more than 5,000 hours of Bravo footage — and, according to NBCU, there are more than 600 billion unique viewing variants. The feeds are assembled using a combination of AI technology and human editors, per NBCU. A key component: Peacock app users can tap directly from a clip into the full episode or season. That’s designed to provide a new front door for content discovery that (ideally) drives long-form viewing, all within a single experience. Your Bravoverse also promises “exclusive, never-before-seen content” from current seasons and the Bravo archive. NBCU also has an advertising play with Your Bravoverse. In addition to sponsoring custom moments and video clips in the Peacock app, NBCU says, Cohen’s avatar can audibly reference a sponsor’s brand. Wendy’s joins as the first sponsor of Your Bravoverse at launch, building on its longstanding relationship with Bravo. NBCU is positioning Your Bravoverse as the latest Peacock feature that differentiates it from other streamers. The app includes real-time vertical highlights and clips, original unscripted microdramas, multiview capabilities, mini-games and other interactive experiences. Why is Peacock leaning into Bravo? It’s a very active fandom: According to the company, in 2026, Bravo superfans watch up to 75 episodes of its shows per month, and BravoCon 2025 drew 30,000 fans in person and 3 million streaming viewers. In addition, Bravo viewers on Peacock watch 92% more non-Bravo content than the platform user average — a key stat that underscores by NBCU kept Bravo in the fold while spinning off its other cable networks like CNBC and USA into Versant Media. NBCU makes all of Bravo’s content available day-after-air on Peacock. The streaming platform also will serve as the exclusive streaming home of Bravo Fan Fest Charleston on Saturday, Oct. 24, featuring live coverage of panels, interviews and behind-the-scenes moments. Ava DuVernay’s timely and viscerally moving “ 14th ” leads this year’s Critics Choice Documentary Awards nominations with six, including best documentary feature. Close behind with five nominations apiece are Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s examination of Elizabeth Holmes, “ You Can See Everything ”; Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman’s polar bear migration story, “Nuisance Bear”; David Greaves’ archival portrait of Black cultural history, “Once Upon a Time in Harlem” and Pegah Ahangarani’s Iranian historical documentary, “Rehearsals for a Revolution.” Related Stories Raindance to Launch U.K.'s First Major Vertical Festival and Market (EXCLUSIVE) Telly Awards Adds Microseries Competition Track, With Dozens of New Categories (EXCLUSIVE) Netflix led all distributors with 17 nominations, nearly double the nine earned by runner-up Neon. Now in its 11th year, the Critics Choice Documentary Awards will take place Nov. 8 at the Edison Ballroom in New York City, with television host and producer Ross Matthews serving as host. The awards celebrate excellence in nonfiction filmmaking. The organization’s track record of predicting Oscar success has been mixed over the years. Its inaugural top prize winner, “O.J.: Made in America” (2016), went on to win the Academy Award for documentary feature. Since then, only three other top prize winners or nominees have crossed over to the Oscars: winner “Summer of Soul (…Or, When the Revolution Could Not Be Televised)” (2021) and nominees “Will & Harper” (2024) and last year’s “The Perfect Neighbor” (2025). All others failed to be nominated, or in some cases, not even make the preliminary shortlist (i.e., 2022’s “Good Night Oppy”). As previously announced, Ron Howard will receive the Critics Choice Impact Award. Visionary filmmaker Jehane Noujaim will receive the CCA’s Pennebaker Award, presented by Chris Hegedus, Pennebaker’s widow and longtime collaborator. Named in honor of trailblazing documentarian D.A. Pennebaker, the award, formerly known as the Critics Choice Lifetime Achievement Award, recognizes filmmakers whose careers have made a profound and lasting contribution to documentary storytelling. Feature-length documentaries, two-part documentaries and short-form documentaries are eligible for nomination if they were first released commercially in the U.S. between Jan. 1 and Dec. 31, 2026. title: Ryan Coogler’s ‘The X-Files’ Reboot Picked Up To Series At Hulu
full_text: Skip to main content By Denise Petski Denise Petski Senior Managing Editor More Stories By Denise Ryan Coogler’s ‘The X-Files’ Reboot Picked Up To Series At Hulu Maddie Hasson Joins Julia Garner & Lewis Pullman In Apple TV’s ‘Guilty Creatures’ Amber Siyavus Dies: ‘Big Brother’ Season 8 Contestant Was 46 View All October 13, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Himesh Patel and Danielle Deadwyler Nat Jamieson/Deadline Ryan Coogler ‘s long-gestating The X-Files reboot, starring Emmy nominee Himesh Patel ( The Odyssey, Station Eleven ) and Danielle Deadwyler ( The Bell Jar, The Chaperones ), has been ordered to series at Hulu . From Onyx Collective and 20th Television, the reimagining of Chris Carter ‘s classic series follows two highly decorated but vastly different FBI agents, played by Deadwyler and Patel, who form an unlikely bond when they are assigned to a long-shuttered division devoted to cases involving unexplained phenomena. Sinners filmmaker Coogler wrote, directed and executive produced the pilot via his Proximity Media. He executive produces with showrunner Jennifer Yale. Executive producers also include Zinzi Coogler and Sev Ohanian for Proximity Media and The X-Files creator Carter. Co-executive producers are Simone Harris for Proximity Media, along with Deadwyler and Patel. Related Stories News 'Bob's Burgers' Sets Premiere For Hulu Holiday Short; Releases First-Look Clip News Himesh Patel & Maxine Peake Among The Stars In Latest Booker Prize Short Films “I’ve loved The X-Files for a long time, so getting the chance to write and direct the pilot has meant a great deal to me,” said Coogler. “What Chris Carter created is special, and we wanted to honor everything that made the original series connect with so many people while also finding our own way into that world. Danielle and Himesh, along with the rest of our cast, have brought such original perspectives and performances to these characters, and watching that come together has been one of the most rewarding parts of the experience. I couldn’t have asked for better collaborators than my crew, colleagues at Proximity Media and our partners at Onyx Collective and 20th Television. I’m grateful for the trust and support they’ve given us as we take on this new chapter.” Watch on Deadline The series order caps a more than three-year journey for the project, which falls under Coogler’s five-year exclusive television deal with Disney , the parent company of Hulu, 20th TV and Onyx. Carter first revealed during a 2023 podcast interview that he had spoken with Coogler who was “going to remount The X Files with a diverse cast,” adding, “He’s got his work cut out for him because we covered so much territory.” “We’re looking forward to continuing this journey as executive producers and especially excited to work closely with Jennifer Yale, Simone Harris, and the entire cast and crew as we bring this new chapter of The X-Files to life,” said Zinzi Coogler, Sev Ohanian and Ryan Coogler, founders of Proximity Media. “It was also incredibly special to have our fellow Proximity co-founder Ludwig Göransson contribute the score for the pilot, making this a true collaboration across the Proximity family.” Carter’s original X-Files starred Gillian Anderson and David Duchovny as FBI Special Agents Dana Scully and Fox Mulder, who investigate cases involving paranormal phenomena. The series premiered on Fox in 1993 and ran for nine seasons. It spawned two feature films, The X-Files (1998) and The X-Files: I Want to Believe (2008), as well as a 2016 revival, which aired on Fox for two seasons. She will star opposite Jeremy Strong in the upcoming six-episode limited series inspired by the David vs. Goliath fight that won justice for 9/11’s ailing heroes. Waterston will play Amy Smith, a lawyer and the soon-to-be ex-wife of Jason (Strong). From writers Tobias Lindholm and Frank Pugliese, the 6-episode series The Best of Us dramatizes a landmark case that reshaped the fight for accountability: a relentless legal war that stretched nearly a decade to secure almost $1 billion in compensation for first responders who fell gravely ill in the wake of 9/11. The guest cast includes LaChanze, Richard Schiff , Elizabeth Rodriguez, Joe Morton, Jen Tullock, William Baldwin, and Keith W. Richards. Produced by Paramount Television Studios and Sister, the limited series is written, directed, and executive produced by Lindholm and written and executive produced by Pugliese. Strong is also an executive producer, along with Tony Hernandez. Waterston was recently seen in Paul Greengrass’ The Uprising and in the Paramount+ series The Agency alongside Michael Fassbender. Additional credits include the latest installment in the Fear Street franchise, Prom Queen, The End We Start From , Slow Horses , Perry Mason , They Listen , Babylon , Inherent Vice , Alien: Covenant, and the Fantastic Beasts film series. title: Fox Boss Rob Wade Commits Long Term To Creator Studios: “We’re Not Here To Flip A House”
full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Channel 4 Unveils First-Ever Microdrama: Female Friendship Series Stars ‘You’s Jadesola Odunjo We Will Never “Lie To The Audience” Over Artificial Intelligence, Says BBC Content Chief Kate Phillips BBC Studios Launches Scripted Fund & Tasks Ben Donald With Helping Unearth Next Generation Of European IP View All October 13, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Rob Wade Banff EXCLUSIVE: Fox Entertainment CEO Rob Wade has committed long into the future to his company’s creator studio, telling Deadline: “We’re not here to flip a house.” Fox Creator Studios (FCS), a “digital-first division,” was unveiled at the start of this year with partnerships including a food roster headed by Gordon Ramsay, but the idea had been percolating in Wade’s mind for more than a decade. Wade feels that plenty of big companies are investing in the creator, AI and tech space simply in order to “sell for hundreds of millions and get out,” but Fox won’t be following suit. “The game is built around that, which is not a recipe for long-term success,” said Wade. “But we’re in it for the long term. We’re not here to flip a house. If I want to invest in something, my bosses and board will say that if it’s successful they want to build on it. We will never sell [Fox Creator Studios].” Related Stories News 'Baywatch' Reboot Full Trailer Release Ahead Of January 2027 Premiere On Fox News The YouTube Age: Meet The Content Creators Making Waves In Europe Wade was speaking to Deadline in the days leading up to MIPCOM , where he has just been joined on a Deadline-hosted panel by FCS boss Billy Parks , Prentiss Fraser, who runs distributor Fox Entertainment Global (FEG), and Fox-backed creators Josh Richards and Chris Sawtelle. Watch on Deadline Wade, Parks and Fraser have grand plans, with the former positioning the main goal as “creating a path to IP creation on the internet.” In this vein, FCS is doing things a bit differently to its rivals in what is becoming an increasingly crowded space both in the U.S. and internationally, with content creators one of the big topics at this year’s MIPCOM, a traditional TV sales market. FCS is seeking to tie with content creators across a whole range of genres but won’t necessarily air their work solely on Fox or Fox-owned platforms like Tubi. Instead, it will leverage resources and advertising infrastructure to create content spanning different platforms and territories. Content creators can then diversify revenue streams, while FEG boss Fraser and her team shop their wares around the world. The studio has so far struck deals with long-time Fox collaborator Ramsay, comedian Tom Segura and creators like Richards, who makes YouTube sketch comedy Read the Room. This approach sets Fox apart from its competitors in two key ways, Wade believes, “going direct and investing in original content by creating finance for new shows,” and providing “very significant advertising infrastructure” via an ad sales division that has the likes of the NFL and World Cup in its portfolio. Parks, who joined Fox from The Chernin Group, said the studio offers hands-off support to creators who are “being pulled in many different directions.” “We’re not greenlighting their ideas through a long, traditional development process,” he added. “Instead, we’re available for notes and feedback in an equitable way, without approaching the relationship as a top-down studio-to-creative model.” In this way, Parks said creators “who are trying to do something outside their comfort zone” can be supported with capital and an IP-sharing vision. “Many platforms that work with creators option their libraries or make shows with them to drive audiences to their own platforms,” he added. “That’s how companies such as Netflix, Amazon and Hulu are structured to work. That isn’t necessarily better or worse. Every creator will make different choices at different points in their career. But those platforms are primarily built to acquire subscribers, and that’s what they do with creators.” Parks was recently at creator economy market VidSummit, where he said bosses at CAA, UTA and WME were all present along with leaders from platforms like Netflix and Tubi. “Everyone is thinking about the different types of deals available to creators, whether that involves investment, production or intellectual property,” he added. All started with ‘Dancing With The Stars’ But while creators may be the talk of today, Wade and Parks have been thinking about this for a long while. Wade says FCS’ inception harks back more than 15 years to when he was a producer on Dancing with the Stars and booked the show’s first ever YouTuber, Bethany Mota. “She did very well but we learned a few things,” he added. “I was expecting an avalanche of YouTube views and imagined the votes for her would heavily skew young but there was no sudden mass of views or a sudden mass on YouTube. Our knowledge of the internet back then was very different.” He realized that YouTube success does not always translate to traditional TV in obvious ways and figured out over the years that a studio’s infrastructure could be used in smart ways in this space. Things solidified with the success of Prime Video and A24’s Hazbin Hotel, which was produced by Fox-owned Bento Box and started life on YouTube via its creator Vivienne Medrano. “We thought to ourselves, ‘We’re not a library, we’re a studio’,” added Wade. “What a studio does is back creators and put bets on them. That is something we know how to do.” White House Press Secretary’s Debut: Very Short, Some News, Much Trump Praise The YouTube Age: Content Creators Making Waves In Europe Toon Comedy ‘Merrick & Treves’ From ‘Archer’ Team Lands Two-Season HBO Order Cranston & Other ‘Breaking Bad’ Alums Mourn Actor Who Played Walt Jr. Read More About: Comments

title: How ‘Breaking Bad’ Actor R.J. Mitte Made an Impact as a Disability Rights Activist
full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 13, 2026 8:49am Add us as a Google Preferred Source R.J. Mitte. Hatnim Lee/Getty Images R.J. Mitte was best known for playing the son of Walter White on the iconic TV drama Breaking Bad . But the actor also held another pivotal role. Mitte did a lot of good off the screen , via his family connected Mitte Foundation and through a host of health non-profits before his unexpected death on Monday. The actor, at age 34, died by suicide in Brownsville, Texas, his rep confirmed to The Hollywood Reporter. Mitte was diagnosed with Cerebral Palsy at age 3. He famously exaggerated his condition while playing Flynn, the son to Walter (played by Bryan Cranston ) and Skyler White (Anna Gunn), for five seasons on the Emmy-winning AMC drama that aired from 2008 to 2013. Mitte used his Breaking Bad platform to challenge stereotypes around people with disabilities. He advocated for greater inclusion as president of The Mitte Foundation , a Texas-based philanthropic organization launched by the late Roy F. Mitte and Joann Cole Mitte, his adoptive parents. In addition to driving disability rights awareness, the family connected foundation also offered scholarships and arts programs, and funded community initiatives. Related Stories TV 'Breaking Bad' Stars Bryan Cranston, Aaron Paul, Others Remember R.J. Mitte: "Sweetheart of a Young Man" TV R.J. Mitte, Walter White's Son on 'Breaking Bad,' Dies at 34 Mitte’s lifelong activism also included being an honorary trustee and spokesperson for United Cerebral Palsy after he was diagnosed with the neurological condition. In a 2015 interview with the BBC , Mitte recalled nabbing the role of Walter “Flynn” White Jr. at age 14 as a disabled actor as a part that “gave me an opportunity to bring light to subjects like this and disabilities that need to be heard and to show people how normal a disability really is.” He made his way to Hollywood by following his younger sister, Lacianne, after she got a job offer to work in film production. He first appeared uncredited a year later on an episode of Hannah Montana , and had early acting roles on 7th Heaven and Weeds. Mitte’s big break came with the Vince Gilligan drama, and his performance on 56 episodes of Breaking Bad drew on his real-life experiences with CP. Mitte also served as an ambassador for the Shriners Children’s nonprofit medical network as he urged more care for children with specialized health needs. The health non-profit supports research to develop new treatments for the benefit of physicians and other healthcare professionals and their patients. Mitte helped fundraise for Shriner’s Children after being treated at Shriners Hospital for Children in Shreveport, Louisiana, after his diagnosis and for most of his childhood to overcome physical and verbal impediments. “I can’t thank Shriners Hospitals for Children enough for what they did to help me overcome the effects of cerebral palsy,” the actor said in a 2014 statement as he joined a Love to the Rescue fundraising campaign. “Had it not been for my doctors and therapists, I would not be walking and talking as well as I am today. I know first-hand that Shriners Hospitals for Children is a special place where kids are given a life of possibilities because they send Love to the rescue every day.” At the 2013 Media Access Awards, Mitte received the SAG-AFTRA Howard Russell Award for his disability activism and portrayal of Walt Jr. That came on top of receiving a Screen Actors Guild Award for best drama ensemble for the final season of Breaking Bad. “Beyond his acting, Mitte advocated for people with disabilities and worked to raise awareness of a variety of conditions while pushing for expanded roles for people with disabilities in Hollywood with disabilities,” SAG-AFTRA said in an Instagram post on news of Mitte’s death. His Breaking Bad co-stars, meanwhile, led the Hollywood tributes that praised both his acting, as well as his activism. “That kid was pretty raw when we started shooting the pilot in February of 2007, but little by little we watched him grow into a really fine actor. He parlayed his experience on the show to be a vocal advocate for performers with disabilities, and was the head of a philanthropic organization with a focus on helping the disabled community,” Cranston shared , in part, in a lengthy post on Instagram. “We were texting each other just a few weeks ago — figuring out when we could meet for lunch. I don’t know if that lunch would have changed his future… But I do know that I loved him, and thoroughly enjoyed being with him throughout the years on the series, and after the spotlight on Breaking Bad dimmed… I’ll miss you,” son.” THR

Related Stories News Josh Schwartz & Stephanie Savage Strike First-Look Deal With Amazon; Barneys New York Drama In The Works With Susan Rovner As EP Cancellations and Renewals ‘Sterling Point’ Renewed For Season 2 By Prime Video Bella from Barneys follows Bella Baldwin, an outer-borough outsider with an eye for style, who lands a job in the stock room of the newly revived Barneys New York. When she talks her way into becoming a personal shopper to the store’s most notorious socialite client, she’s pulled into a cutthroat world of fashion and family secrets, and into the orbit of the heir fighting to save the family business. Deadline revealed the project was in development last year as part of a new first-look deal between Amazon MGM Studios and Schwartz and Savage. Barneys was a New York institution; a high-end department store that was founded in 1923. In 2024, there was also a pop-up Barneys in Soho. Josh Schwartz & Stephanie Savage (Jason Mendez/Getty) “We’re thrilled to be continuing our partnership with Amazon and are excited for what’s ahead,” said Schwartz and Savage. “The response to Sterling Point has been incredibly gratifying, and we’re so happy to be returning for a second season alongside creator Megan Park and producing partners LuckyChap. We’re so excited to open those doors along with our partners at Authentic Brands Group, and our fellow producers Susan Rovner and Rachel Kaplan, who we have worked with since the beginning of our careers.” “Josh and Stephanie at Fake Empire have this rare gift for creating worlds that feel both electric and cozy all at once, and Bella from Barneys is a perfect example,” added Peter Friedlander, Head of Global Television, Amazon MGM Studios. “Barneys New York was more than a department store — it was a fashion institution, and when it closed, people genuinely mourned it. This series brings it roaring back to life in all its impossibly chic glory. Fashion, ambition, and intrigue await inside the doors that our partners Susan, Rachel, and the team at Authentic Brands Group will help reopen.” “At Authentic, our brands are stories, and Bella from Barneys shows what’s possible when iconic IP meets world-class storytelling. We’re excited to bring its legacy to the screen with Fake Empire. Josh Schwartz and Stephanie Savage, who are unmatched at creating stylish, character-driven drama, are the perfect stewards for the Barneys brand,” said Corey Salter, CEO Entertainment, Authentic. title: ‘Queen Silvia’ Ditches the Glass Slipper for Un-Cinderella Royal Romance
full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All October 13, 2026 8:40am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Queen Silvia' Amazon-Joyn-Pyjama-Pictures Every royal romance eventually gets the Cinderella treatment: the humble girl, the dashing prince, the ball, the happily-ever-after. Not so Queen Silvia . The new European aristocratic romance, which has its world premiere at international TV conference Mipcom tonight , ditches the fairy tale for a more realistic take on an ordinary girl who finds her prince. The six-hour limited series, produced by Berlin’s Pyjama Pictures with Sweden’s Unlimited Stories, follows the real-life romance between Silvia Sommerlath, a German-Brazilian interpreter working at the 1972 Munich Olympics, and Sweden’s Crown Prince Carl Gustaf, the games’ guest of honor. Their first meet cut is cut short by a terrorist attack — the Black September attacks on the Israeli team. Silvia holds her own under pressure, and the prince is smitten. But Silvia is not quite ready to trade her career for a tiara. Related Stories TV The Asylum Is Bringing 'Z Nation' Back From the Dead (Exclusive) Movies Amsterdam's IDFA Sets Int'l, Envision Competition Lineups, Adds 'Musk,' 'You Can See Everything' “Silvia is not a woman who wants to become queen,” series director Miguel Alexandre tells The Hollywood Reporter . “She was a very independent woman, following a great career, and was not at all impressed by all this royal baggage. But she falls in love with a man who brings this baggage with him.” “She was such a powerhouse herself already at such a young age, very independent,” says German actress Alicia von Rittberg, star of Charité and Becoming Elizabeth , who plays Silvia. “It was a struggle for her, to fit in with the royal world, to make that work.” Starting from 1970s Munich, the series carries through to the couple’s 1976 wedding, an event made world famous for its soundtrack. Swedish supergroup ABBA composed their hit “Dancing Queen” as a wedding gift for Queen Silvia, and performed the song live at a televised gala on June 18, 1976, the night before the royal wedding. Beta Film, which is selling Queen Silvia worldwide, leaned into the ABBA connection at Mipcom , hiring German-US singer Caro Kelley to perform a live version of “Dancing Queen” both at the company’s Beta Brunch sales event, at at the series’ world premiere gala. Swedish actor Edvin Endre ( Vikings , Fortitude , Eddie the Eagle ), who plays Carl Gustaf in the series, says Queen Silvia ‘s “more realistic, more grounded” take on the monarchy, could be a revelation for Swedes as well, who often view their King Gustaf in a less-than-favorable light. “When [the King] is portrayed, it’s usually as the butt of the joke,” says Endre. “He’s presented as being silly, goofy, not all that smart. I don’t think that’s the truth at all. I think he takes his job very seriously. So for this role, I wanted to go in the opposite direction.” Endre points to the king’s dyslexia as the root of the teasing. “Whenever he would give speeches from a very young age, he would stumble and he would struggle, and this is kind of the reason why people don’t take him seriously,” he says. “People were so brutal to him in the press.” The show’s approach, he says, is “a lot of sympathy and… making him as human as possible.” Endre describes the story of the two 20-somethings as being as much “a coming-of-age story” as a royal romance. “At the end of the day, they’re two young people sitting alone in a palace, trying to figure out each other and like if they can go on this journey together…being scared and being in love and all that stuff.” Adds Von Rittberg: “and both of them are trying to break free from the expectations of their parents.” Making a drama about a living king and queen is a risky business, as the show’s producers are well aware. Alexandre says Unlimited kept the Swedish court informed at every stage in the production, but that the royal family did not ask to participate. When asked about the show, the king said publicly that making a series about them while they are still alive was “a horrible idea.” But Endre is quick to allay fears that Queen Silvia is a hatchet job. “Everyone involved in this has really approached this project with a lot of like integrity and love and respect,” he says. He calls the real couple “the most progressive royals in the world,” who “really changed the monarchy in Sweden, made it more relevant and more approachable.” The royal family, however, will not be in attendance for Queen Silvia ‘s Mipcom premiere. The producers say the court was informed of the screening and replied with a curt “thanks and good luck.” A screener was also offered. No word yet on whether anyone is clearing a spot on the royal couch. THR

title: ‘Crystal Lake’ Review: Peacock’s Linda Cardellini-Starring Series Is the Best ‘Friday the 13th’ Property Yet (Which Isn’t Saying a Lot)
