Matt Infante/PEACOCK Logo text As somebody who spent countless hours in the ’90s trawling Blockbuster shelves with friends looking for or awaiting the return of Friday the 13th entries we hadn’t seen, or hadn’t seen recently — my apologies for the wasted time, guys — it gives me no pleasure to admit that “What is the best Friday the 13th movie?” is a trick question. Unlike the Halloween and Nightmare on Elm Street franchises, there’s no clear prestige Friday the 13th film — just minor gradations in the quality of makeup effects or the creativity of the kills. I appreciate The Final Chapter for the weirdness of Crispin Glover’s performance, Part III for the hilarious vestigial 3-D effects, and even Part II because director Steven Miner knew where to put the camera, which can’t be said for all of his successors. Related Stories TV 'Crystal Lake' Will Offer More Brutal Kills Than Films, Go Deep on Jason's Background TV Alexander Brothers' Sex Trafficking Trial Tackled in Peacock's 'Wolves of Real Estate' Trailer Crystal Lake The Bottom Line Bloody well exceeds the low bar set by the movies. Airdate: Thursday, October 15 (Peacock) Cast: Linda Cardellini, William Catlett, Davin Kessler, Cameron Scoggins, Gwendolyn Sunstrom Developed by: Brad Caleb Kane Still, it was possible to assume that Peacock ‘s Crystal Lake would be the best entry in the franchise; the presence of Linda Cardellini getting eight hours to play Pamela Voorhees generated hopes for a level of quality none of the earlier films could muster, with or without such tantalizing revelations as “Where Jason’s mother got that spectacular sweater.” Indeed, thanks to newly minted Emmy winner Cardellini, giving the best Friday the 13th -adjacent performance to date, Crystal Lake lives up to that very reasonable level of potential. Is the series beyond Cardellini any good? It’s hard to always say. Following a template that eventually worked extremely well on A&E’s Bates Motel , occasionally well in Amazon’s newly released Carrie and barely at all on Netflix’s Ratched , Crystal Lake deserves some credit for taking a narrative expansion that could have been silly and making it earnest and nuanced, albeit in familiar prestige TV ways. But that also means that Crystal Lake takes itself more seriously than its auspices demand or can justify. Most of the episodes run at least 50 minutes and, after a fairly promising start, there’s a multi-episode lag before a season-closing rush of episodes that include a wild reconfiguring of the events of the first movie, as well as a wholly original flashback installment that plays like the bizarre love child of David Cronenberg and Douglas Sirk. Ultimately, Crystal Lake is better than it needed to be, occasionally because it’s twisted, gory fun and occasionally just because of the easy comfort of low expectations. After an in medias res introduction with Cardellini’s Pamela starring at herself in the mirror, drenched in blood, the story goes back nine months and we’re introduced to a cleaner Pamela working the kitchen at Camp Crystal Lake in New Jersey. Initially, camp is heaven for 11-year-old Jason Voorhees (Callum Vinson). Jason has a variety of birth defects that cause the cruel campers to make fun of him, but he does have one friend, fellow outcast Grace (Gwendolyn Sundstrom). He also has the doting love of Pamela, who tries to be a constant presence in Jason’s life and even gets him a mail-order box of camping supplies like a tent, nature cooking provisions and a machete. “You use it to clear brush and get rid of obstacles, make your own path,” Pamela explains helpfully, a line of dialogue most viewers are likely to miss because of the maniacal giggles elicited by “How Jason Voorhees Got His First Machete” origin story. Things do not work out well for poor Jason, who isn’t a very good swimmer to begin with — his malformed head makes him buoyancy-challenged — and then goes on an unsupervised swim. Why does he lack supervision? Because counselors Claudette (Danielle Kotch) and Barry (Phoenix Panevik) chose to go to a barn for nookie rather than watching their campers. Bad decision, Claudette and Barry. Back in the present day, which is actually 1971 or 1972, we see a distracted and grieving Pamela. The community of Crystal Lake wants to be supportive, especially Levon ( William Catlett ), a widower with a dark past and big ole crush on Pamela and her exceptional sweater. Levon, the local sheriff, wants Pamela to bowl and go to town picnics, but Pamela can’t move forward — especially since Jason’s body was never retrieved after his drowning. For a while, Crystal Lake hews closely to the very rudimentary mythology introduced in Sean Cunningham’s original movie. It’s structured so that dedicated fans are able to point in happy recognition at town landmarks, the architecture of the camp and the appearance of familiar characters including Ralph (Nick Cordileone), the crazy “Don’t go to Crystal Lake!” guy in the movies, now a Vietnam veteran suffering from serious PTSD. Then strange things start happening that don’t align with anything in the movies, including the arrival of two threatening men who show up asking questions about Pamela’s past and bring out the worst — or best, since Pamela Voorhees: Non-Violent Lunch Lady is not a show anybody would have watched — in our heroine. For a while, Crystal Lake suffers from many of the same issues that plagued the first season of Bates Motel — namely, a whole lot of incongruous elements that don’t even feel thematically connected to the things (hockey masks, nudity) that resonate about the movies. It feels like series developer Brad Caleb Kane is throwing random things against the wall, particularly seeding elements for a vast conspiracy that’s like something out of a half-dozen Stephen King novels rather than Friday the 13th . There’s a dogged journalist (Devin Kessler as Levon’s sister, Briana), who serves no purpose for a long time. Even when she becomes useful, it’s in a complementary way that could have very nearly been removed from the story entirely. There’s even a full episode set at an EST-style retreat, an over-extended if amusing gag suggesting that Pamela’s road to empowerment reaches a fork at which she has to choose between harmless self-actualizing platitudes or chopping negligent counselors to bits. I didn’t mind the EST episode, because it’s one of the moments that the series’ early-’70s setting pays off. It doesn’t quite make Pamela Voorhees into a feminist icon, but if you set your story in the days of Manson-inspired paranoia, Nixon-inspired institutional distrust and a burgeoning ERA ratification movement, the extreme reaction of a doting mother struggling to raise and then mourn her special needs child gains some resonance. The early episodes have a gritty, grindhouse-friendly look, with washed-out colors and grimy, dilapidated cars and exteriors. Michael Lennox, whose credits run the wide gamut from Derry Girls to Say Nothing , strikes an interesting balance among grounded realism, campy performances, gloomy settings, cheery soundtrack choices and wildly extreme violence. Very extreme. People in Crystal Lake are constantly being dispatched in ways that offer the most shredded flesh, spurting blood and oozing viscera possible. Why simply stab somebody when you could flay their face off and then do something even more disgusting to finish the job, before disposing of the body in an additional nasty way? It’s my instinct that more of the violence is CG-driven than practical, but if you come to Crystal Lake hoping to go “Ew!” and episodes require you to sit around for 45 minutes during which nothing happens, at least the kills should deliver. And they do. Without spoiling much, it’s the sixth and then seventh episodes directed by duo Celine Held and Logan George and then former cinematographer Quyen Tran that kick the show into a higher gear before an okay finale. The flashback episode, with a color scheme and overall tone lifted from 1950s melodramas and 1970s conspiracy thrillers, was the one hour I found myself wholly and unapologetically loving Crystal Lake , as opposed to mostly being curious about what the spine of the show would be once the homages ran dry. The primary reason to keep watching is Cardellini, who makes Pamela her own with few traces of Betsy Palmer’s fine, very broad work in the first film. Cardellini plays her as a strong but brittle woman, looking for a purpose without the child she built her life around, but always right on the edge of going to pieces. Don’t worry, the breakdown starts in a hurry and Cardellini is terrifying, if perhaps not as sympathetic as the series requires long-term. Fortunately, Sundstrom generates enough sympathy on her own, giving a sweet and vulnerable performance as the only Crystal Lake character you really don’t want to see die. Kotch and Parnevik, as the negligently canoodling counselors, inspire the opposite reaction as two characters whose destiny is inevitable and earned. Catlett’s character is an arbitrary addition to the series, and I never cared what his secret was from his days as a cop in Newark, but the actor is an assertive screen presence and there’s borderline sweetness to the flirtations between him and Pamela, two damaged souls. Other standouts include Manon Gage as a trouble-making hippie; a very hungry brown bear; Joy Suprano as a budding feminist who befriends Pamela; and a prolific TV presence who guest stars in the second half of the season. That’s already more standout performances than in the entire run of films, a reminder that working with trashy IP is a safer bet than attempting to embellish a classic. (Of course, Bates Motel got better and better as it went along, even though it got closer and closer to the key events from Psycho .) Crystal Lake may already have moved beyond the parts of the Friday the 13th franchise that made me keep watching film after film without thinking any of them was truly “good.” So even though the seeds planted for future seasons don’t fill me with optimism for more Crystal Lake , my low expectations have already been exceeded once. THR

title: From ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ to a Stick-Figure YouTuber: THR’s First Animation Power List
full_text: × Skip to main content (L to R): 'Wildwood,' 'K-Pop: Demon Hunters,' 'Simpsons' creator Matt Groening, 'Acme vs. Coyote' Laika, Netflix, Fox, Ketchup Entertainment Animation has never been bigger or more difficult to pin down. In the past year alone, a K-pop-fueled Netflix phenomenon swept the Oscars, a Chinese sequel became the highest-grossing animated film of all time and a stick-figure animator built an audience of 34 million-plus without ever setting foot in a studio. Meanwhile, a family of Australian blue heelers is teaching parents around the world how to raise their kids. Animation’s center of gravity isn’t just shifting — it’s multiplying. THR Which is why The Hollywood Reporter is launching its first-ever Animation Power List, a representative snapshot of the most important and influential figures working in animation today, across film, television and online. Box office and ratings matter, of course, and plenty of the names here have the billions to prove it. But commercial success is only part of the equation. We also weighed the more subjective, harder-to-quantify question of influence: Who is setting the aesthetic agenda, shaping the business models, launching new talent or simply making the rest of the industry look over its shoulder? We tried to strike a balance, pairing the studio heads and A-list directors who steer the biggest projects with the character designers, animators, FX supervisors and art directors whose craft, all too often, goes unsung. This is a snapshot, not a definitive ranking or a comprehensive census. In a business this big and this global, someone is bound to have been unjustly left off. To those we missed: We’re sorry, we’re big fans and there’s always next year. Consider this an opening sketch. Eric Bauza Image Credit: Storm-Santos Voice Actor ( Coyote vs. Acme, Teen Titans Go! ) Bauza has quietly become the voice of an entire cartoon universe. One of the successors to the legendary Mel Blanc as the voice of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Marvin the Martian and a dozen more iconic characters, the Canadian actor outdid himself with Coyote vs. Acme , voicing everything from Bugs Bunny to Foghorn Leghorn and Tweety Bird. Says Bauza: “A lot of talented folks worked really hard to make this film, and to be able to see it celebrated by so many people across the globe has really made the wait worth it.” Alan Becker, aka Noogai Animator/Influencer Becker built an empire out of stick figures. The self-taught animator behind Animator vs. Animation — known to 34 million-plus YouTube subscribers as Noogai — Becker turned a scrappy Flash experiment into a launchpad for a new kind of animation career, one built on tutorials, software tools and brand collaborations rather than a studio contract. Eric Beckman Image Credit: Leon Bennett/Getty Images CEO, GKIDS Beckman has brought international indie animation to the American mainstream, from The Secret of Kells and The Breadwinner to the Studio Ghibli catalog. GKIDS has built an audience, and an awards platform, for non-Hollywood animation, creating a sustainable distribution model for ambitious features made outside the major studios. Kristine Belson & Damien de Froberville Image Credit: SonyPicturesAnimation Presidents, Sony Pictures Animation Sony Pictures Animation’s presidents are having a moment. Belson oversaw the development and production of Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse , Sony’s first best animated feature Oscar winner, then, after de Froberville joined as president in 2025, conquered the world with KPop Demon Hunters . The duo say their proudest moment of 2026 is the commercial success of sports comedy GOAT : “Seeing audiences embrace an original story with such a distinctive point of view has been enormously gratifying.” Brad Bird Director ( The Incredibles , Iron Giant , Ray Gunn ) Bird doesn’t make small movies. The Oscar-winning director has spent decades proving animation can carry the same emotional and visual weight as any big-budget tentpole. After stints at Pixar and Disney, Bird returned to original feature animation this year with sci-fi noir Ray Gunn for Netflix, a passion project 30 years in the making. Brad Bird’s Ray Gunn hits theaters Dec. 4 and will be available on Netflix on Dec. 18. Skydance Animation/Netflix Jared Bush Image Credit: Disney Animation Studios Chief Creative Officer, Walt Disney Animation Studios Bush has become a key creative force shaping the next phase of Disney Animation. Under his leadership, the studio is expanding established franchises while developing new original features, including the upcoming Hexed . His latest effort behind the camera, on Zootopia 2 , which grossed $1.87 billion worldwide, wasn’t too shabby either. Enrico Casarosa Image Credit: Deborah Coleman / Pixar Director ( Luca , Gatto ) Italian-born auteur Casarosa first caught the world’s attention with the lyrical Pixar short La Luna , a visual poem about family rituals set against a moonlit seascape. Casarosa’s style, which brings the warmth, looseness and imperfection of hand-drawn illustration into 3D animation, will be on full display in his upcoming feature, the animated gangster comedy Gatto . The film will be Pixar’s big spring release of 2027. Arden Cho, May Hong & Ji-young Yoo Image Credit: Courtesy of Netflix Voice Actors ( KPop Demon Hunters ) In 2025, KPop Demon Hunters didn’t just become Netflix’s biggest movie of all time, it also turned Cho, Hong and Yoo, as Rumi, Mira and Zoey of fictional K-pop girl group Huntrix, into a genuine voice-cast phenomenon (with EJAE, Audrey Nuna and Rei Ami singing the Huntrix tracks). Cho’s combination of confidence and vulnerability, Hong’s sardonic self-assurance, and Yoo’s playful energy and comic timing combine into a chemistry that couldn’t have worked without all three. Sean Clarke Image Credit: Aardman Animations Managing Director, Aardman Animations Clarke runs the studio that refuses to give up the clay. As managing director of Aardman Animations, he’s kept the British stop-motion house behind Wallace & Gromit , Shaun the Sheep and Chicken Run in business without losing the handmade charm that’s kept audiences coming back for decades (Aardman celebrates its 50th anniversary this year). What would Clarke love to have made in the past year? “It would have to be Toy Story 5 ,” he says. “I worked at Disney when the first film was released and thought it was groundbreaking both in terms of its technique and storytelling.” Pierre Coffin Image Credit: Alex J. Berliner/ABImages Director ( Despicable Me , Minions ) The French director and co-creator of Despicable Me — who came up with the Minions’ multilingual nonsense language and still voices all the little yellow men — has built one of the world’s most successful animated franchises on slapstick timing and character design alone. Coffin continues to develop new animated concepts, but the Minions remain his calling card. Banana! Margie Cohn Image Credit: Alex J. Berliner/ABImages) President, DreamWorks Animation Since taking over as president in 2019, Cohn has pushed DreamWorks toward a broader creative slate and greater stylistic diversity, supporting films such as The Wild Robot . She has argued for a studio without a single house style, emphasizing distinctive filmmaker-driven approaches across both original films and established franchises. Joel Crawford, Januel Mercado Image Credit: Music-Factory Directors ( Forgotten Island ) Crawford and Mercado have been creative collaborators since meeting as storyboard artists on Kung Fu Panda 2 , their shared sensibility for broad comedy, kinetic action and character-driven storytelling finding expression in their work together on The Croods: A New Age and the Oscar-nominated Puss in Boots: The Last Wish . Forgotten Island , their first original feature as writers/directors, stylistically combines 3D CGI with expressive 2D shifts inspired by 1990s anime. Bill Damaschke Image Credit: VALERIE MACON/AFP via Getty Images President & Chief Creative Officer, Warner Bros. Pictures Animation Damaschke is leading Warner Bros. Pictures Animation’s theatrical comeback after a turbulent stretch of shelved projects ( The Day the Earth Blew Up , Coyote vs. Acme ). At Annecy this year, he unveiled a new studio logo and a seven-film slate that starts with the long-awaited The Cat in the Hat feature. “[This year] marks a defining milestone for Warner Bros. Pictures Animation,” says Damaschke. “After three and a half years of building this studio from the ground up, we finally get to share what we’ve been creating with the world!” The Disability Loop Group Image Credit: The Disability Loop Group Voice & Sound Artists The collective of disabled voice actors, singers and sound artists was formed in 2025 through the Easterseals Disability Film Challenge, which advocates for disability inclusion in the entertainment industry. This year they made history on Sony Pictures Animation’s GOAT , becoming the first disability loop group to work on a major studio production. “Having so many talented, disabled voiceover artists working on GOAT was our proudest achievement,” says Nic Novicki, who set up the Disability Loop Group (and is a member) through a partnership with the EDFC. Jaiden Dittfach YouTube Animator Dittfach turned her own life into a cartoon and built an audience of more than 15 million subscribers doing it. Since launching Jaiden Animations on YouTube in 2014, she’s pioneered a format that mixes autobiographical storytelling with whimsical illustration, expanding from web series into merchandise, live events and brand collaborations — proof of how far creator-driven animation can travel. Pete Docter Image Credit: Deborah Coleman / Pixar) Chief Creative Officer, Pixar Animation Studios With three Oscars and a body of work that has redefined what emotional storytelling can look like in animation, Docter needs no introduction. As Pixar’s chief creative officer since 2018, he’s overseen the studio’s next wave, balancing new voices and IP — with the likes of Elio and Hoppers — with careful curation of the studio’s blockbuster franchises. Jennifer Dodge Image Credit: Paramount Animation President, Paramount Animation Since taking over Paramount Animation in January, amid the shake-up that accompanied the studio’s $8 billion merger with Skydance, Dodge has quickly moved to build her own slate, drawing on the experience, at PAW Patrol producer Spin Master, of developing, producing and expanding global franchises. She has moved forward with a wide range of new titles, including Robert Rodriguez’s original Christmas feature The Naughty List , Dan Trachtenberg’s animated horror comedy Freddy the 13th and Bollywood-set animated musical Diya from Nitya Mehra. Holly Edwards Image Credit: Alex J. Berliner/ABImages President, Skydance Animation Edwards joined Skydance in 2019 after two decades at DreamWorks working on such global juggernauts as Kung Fu Panda and How to Train Your Dragon . Under her watch, Skydance’s Swapped became one of Netflix’s biggest animated hits, while Brad Bird’s Ray Gunn , also released by Netflix, is leading this season’s awards conversation. Matt Groening Image Credit: ©2004 THE SIMPSONS and TCFFC ©2004FOX BROADCASTING CO. Creator ( The Simpsons , Futurama ) Groening changed what animation could be on American television, and The Simpsons is still proving it. The longest-running primetime scripted series in TV history hit its 800th episode in February and, thanks to Disney+’s library of all 37 completed seasons, a new generation is being introduced to Bart, Maggie, Lisa, Marge and Homer. (A new Simpsons film is set for 2027.) What Groening did for the family sitcom, he repeated for sci-fi with Futurama , which is set to finish its revived Hulu run with three extended specials next year, and with fantasy with Disenchantment on Netflix. Animation’s living legend says he is not worried about an AI-dominated future. “I, for one, welcome our new A.I. overlords,” Groening says. “I’d like to remind them that, as a trusted TV personality, I can be helpful in rounding up others to toil in their underground data caves.” Jorge R. Gutierrez Image Credit: Vivien Killilea/Getty Images for IMDb Director ( Maya and the Three ) Gutierrez has spent his career putting Mexican folklore front and center in his animation, from the Guillermo del Toro-produced feature The Book of Life to Netflix’s Maya and the Three . Now he’s bringing that sensibility to Speedy Gonzales , the Warner Bros. Pictures Animation feature he is developing to reimagine the classic Looney Tunes character for a modern, more culturally attuned audience. Mark Henn Image Credit: Photofest 2D Animator Henn’s fingerprints are on some of the most iconic hand-drawn characters in Disney history — Ariel, Belle, Aladdin, Mulan — and he has been a key figure in linking the studio’s 2D past with its CGI present, serving as consultant on projects from Frozen to Big Hero 6 to Ralph Breaks the Internet . Takeshi Honda Image Credit: Courtesy of GKIDS Animation Director ( Neon Genesis Evangelion , The Boy and the Heron ) Honda is the animator’s animator, equally adept at crafting epic action sequences — see his work on the Neon Genesis Evangelion series — and subtle, emotional scenes with delicate human figures, a trait the great Hayao Miyazaki relied on when he brought Honda in as animation director on his 2024 Oscar winner The Boy and the Heron . Mike Judge Creator ( Beavis and Butt-Head , King of the Hill ) Judge has been animation’s sharpest cultural barometer since Beavis and Butt-Head first premiered on MTV back in the early ’90s. But his animation legacy arguably sits on the shoulders of King of the Hill , the Texas-set family comedy, rebooted last year, which somehow manages to bridge the political divide while being heartfelt and deeply funny. Maggie Kang & Chris Appelhans Image Credit: The Chosunilbo JNS/Imazins via Getty Images Directors ( KPop Demon Hunters ) Kang and Appelhans cemented their arrival as major animation players with 2025 phenom KPop Demon Hunters , which combined American 3D CGI style with elements of anime and Korean aeni to become a two-time Oscar winner and Netflix’s most watched film of all time. Jin Kim Image Credit: Courtesy of Jin Kim/Disney Character Designer ( Frozen , Zootopia ) Kim worked on Elsa’s visual development in Frozen and supervised character design on Big Hero 6 . His work across Wreck-It Ralph and Moana , Zootopia , Encanto , Strange World and more helped define Disney’s contemporary approach to characters. As the first Korean animator to work at Disney, his career also marked an important opening for Korean artists at the studio. Travis Knight Image Credit: Roy Rochlin/Getty Images President & CEO, Laika Knight has pushed stop-motion into spectacular new territory through 3D-printed facial animation and elaborate action, earning Oscar nominations for producing The Boxtrolls and directing Kubo and the Two Strings and Missing Link . His new feature, Wildwood , promises to take stop-motion places it’s never been before. Hikaru Kondo Image Credit: Koyoharu Gotouge/Sony Pictures Releasing/Courtesy Everett Collection CEO, Ufotable Kondo has overseen Ufotable’s transformation into one of anime’s most globally recognized names. The 2020 release Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — The Movie: Mugen Train was Japan’s highest-grossing film ever, taking in more than $500 million worldwide, a feat topped by 2025’s Infinity Castle , which has earned more than $790 million, confirming anime’s arrival in the global mainstream. Anthony Leo CEO, Cartoon Saloon Leo hasn’t changed much about the animation being done at the Kilkenny-based studio set up by Tomm Moore, Nora Twomey and Paul Young back in 1999. The outfit behind Oscar nominees The Secret of Kells , Song of the Sea and Wolfwalkers is still making hand-drawn tales steeped in the stories and aesthetics of Celtic folklore. Leo has been expanding its global reach, forging co-production deals with the likes of Netflix and Apple TV. Phil Lord & Chris Miller Image Credit: Eric Charbonneau/Getty Images Producers & Directors ( The Lego Movie , Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse ) Lord and Miller have helped rewrite the rules of mainstream CG animation, with pop culture savvy and an anarchic approach to visual storytelling, from Cloudy With a Chance of Meatballs and The Lego Movie to the groundbreaking, Oscar-winning Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse , which pushed animation pipelines and comic book aesthetics further than most thought possible. Filippo Maccari Image Credit: Filippo Maccari FX Supervisor, Sony Pictures Imageworks Maccari’s visual effects work has powered some of the decade’s most striking animated films, from the Oscar-winning Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse and its sequel, to KPop Demon Hunters . His command of particle simulation, lighting and compositing turns ambitious director visions into fully realized worlds. Seth MacFarlane Image Credit: Pamela-Littky Creator & EP ( Family Guy , American Dad! ) MacFarlane built a media empire out of Family Guy , American Dad! and, through his Fuzzy Door banner, a willingness to push every boundary in sight. Family Guy premiered its 24th season on Fox this year, with a milestone 450th episode, and American Dad! hit 400. “I’m really not involved over there. I should probably send them a taco truck or something,” quips MacFarlane. Ted: The Animated Series , a spin-off of MacFarlane’s feature film franchise, hits Peacock Dec. 17, and he has a new Family Guy spinoff, Stewie , which received a two-season order for Fox and Hulu, starting for the 2027-28 season. As a voiceover artist, MacFarlane has a record-tying four Emmy wins for outstanding voiceover performance. But his proudest work achievement of the past year? “Despite all the temptation, never even coming close to starting a podcast.” Vivienne Medrano, aka VivziePop Image Credit: Ilya S. Savenok/Getty Images for Prime Video Animator ( Hazbin Hotel , Helluva Boss ) Medrano, aka VivziePop, has become one of the breakout creators of the online animation boom, turning her self-produced 2019 YouTube pilot for Hazbin Hotel into a global adult animation franchise, partnering with A24 and Bento Box Entertainment to turn it into a Prime Video series. At Annecy, Medrano announced she will make her feature debut with Prehistoria , an original animated musical, which Warner Bros. will produce. Chris Meledandri Image Credit: Alex J. Berliner/ABImages Founder & CEO, Illumination Meledandri has built Illumination Entertainment into one of the industry’s most profitable animation studios on the back of hits from Despicable Me and Minions to Sing and The Super Mario Bros. Movie . Meledandri’s cost-efficient, data-driven production model has kept the studio’s development cycles fast and its merchandising machine humming, while still providing space for individual creative expression. Yvett Merino Image Credit: Dan Abraham Producer ( Moana 2 , Zootopia 2 , Hexed ) Merino made animation history by becoming the first Latina producer to win the Oscar for best animated feature ( Encanto ), and the first animation producer ever to have back-to-back billion-dollar hits (with Moana 2 and Zootopia 2 ). Disney’s hit machine is looking to continue her run with the upcoming original film Hexed , which comes out in November. Hannah Minghella Image Credit: Hannah-Minghella Head, Netflix Animation Minghella oversaw Netflix’s biggest-ever animated hit with two-time Oscar winner KPop Demon Hunters , produced with Sony Pictures Animation, and helped shepherd through the summer hit Swapped and Brad Bird’s Ray Gunn , both with Skydance. Her upcoming slate includes Steps , a revisionist take on Cinderella, and the Roald Dahl spinoff Charlie vs. the Chocolate Factory . Hayao Miyazaki Image Credit: Photo by Steve Granitz/WireImage Director ( Spirited Away , The Boy and the Heron ) Miyazaki, the great master of Japanese animation and co-founder of Studio Ghibli, has built, after only perhaps Walt Disney, animation’s most influential body of work. Miyazaki films have set a global standard for lush hand-drawn animation, richly painted backgrounds and worlds that balance fantasy with deeply human stories. Officially retired or not, Miyazaki’s influence on the medium remains enormous. Japanese animation legend Hayao Miyazaki hired veteran Takeshi Honda for The Boy and the Heron, which won the best animated feature Oscar in 2024. Courtesy of Toho Manabu Otsuka Image Credit: Daniel Zuchnik/Getty Images for Sony Pictures CEO, MAPPA Since becoming president of MAPPA in 2016, Otsuka has built the Japanese anime studio into a global powerhouse, with such crossover hits as Jujutsu Kaisen and Chainsaw Man , whose feature spinoff Chainsaw Man — The Movie: Reze Arc , directed by Tatsuya Yoshihara, was a surprise cross over hit, earning more than $43 million domestically and $162 million worldwide. MAPPA marked its 15th anniversary this year with an expanded strategic partnership with Netflix aimed at developing and distributing new anime globally. Nick Park Image Credit: ©MattCrockett Director ( Wallace & Gromit , Chicken Run ) Park’s painstakingly crafted Oscar-winning shorts — Creature Comforts , The Wrong Trousers and A Close Shave — turned Aardman Animations’ handmade aesthetic into an international signature, while Chicken Run , co-directed with Peter Lord, showed that clay animation could power a major theatrical feature, grossing more than $220 million worldwide. Park remains an executive director at Aardman, where his influence extends through a generation of animators. On the subject of AI, Park is measured but firm: “We at Aardman must stick to our values. It will always be about the human touch for us.” Trey Parker & Matt Stone Image Credit: Leon Bennett/Getty Images Creators ( South Park ) Parker and Stone rewired adult animation with South Park , pioneering a rapid production model that allows the show to turn around topical satire while events are still unfolding. That approach has taken on new relevance in the Trump era , as the series has repeatedly used its speed and anything-goes irreverence to tackle Trump, his administration, political polarization, media pressure and the increasingly blurred line between politics and spectacle. Daley Pearson & Charlie Aspinwall Image Credit: Charlie Aspinwall, Daley Pearson Co-Founders/Directors, Ludo Studio Pearson and Aspinwall’s Ludo Studio turned an Australian blue heeler into a global children’s entertainment phenomenon with Bluey , whose warm, sharply observed depiction of family life has earned two International Emmy Awards and made the Brisbane-based studio one of Australia’s most successful animation exporters. A special mention has to go to Bluey creator Joe Brumm, who stepped away from the series in 2024 to focus on the upcoming Bluey movie, set to hit theaters Aug. 6, 2027. Marc du Pontavice Image Credit: Sameer AL-DOUMY / AFP via Getty Images Founder, Xilam Du Pontavice built Xilam into one of Europe’s most durable animation exporters, launching the French studio in the mid-1990s and steering it toward family-friendly slapstick hits like Oggy and the Cockroaches and Zig & Sharko , as well as the Oscar-nominated I Lost My Body and Zack Snyder’s Norse mythology series Twilight of the Gods for Netflix. Marci Proietto Image Credit: Courtesy of Subject Head, 20th TV Animation Proietto’s tenure has been defined by extending the commercial life of animation’s biggest franchises across broadcast and streaming: In 2025, she helped secure unprecedented four-season renewals for The Simpsons , Family Guy and Bob’s Burgers , while bringing American Dad! back to Fox through the 2028-29 season. Says Proietto: “After 30 years in the business, getting to work alongside the best teams in animation is, hands down, what I’m proudest of.” Chris & Shannon Prynoski Co-Founders, President and Co-President, Titmouse Chris and Shannon Prynoski turned a T-shirt company they launched in 2000 into Titmouse, one of the most distinctive independent forces in contemporary animation. From Metalocalypse to The Legend of Vox Machina , the Prynoskis have built a studio, now with more than 700 employees in L.A., New York, Vancouver and Paris, that has repeatedly given animators room to experiment across styles, genres and platforms, proving that an animation company can operate at scale without adopting a conventional studio identity. Rahul Purini Image Credit: Crunchyroll President, Crunchyroll Once a niche anime streaming service, Crunchyroll, under Purini’s leadership, has become a major force in the U.S. entertainment business and done more than pretty much anyone else to bring Japanese animation directly into the American mainstream. Crunchyroll’s release of Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — Infinity Castle became the highest-grossing anime film ever in the U.S., earning more than $136 million stateside. Chris Sanders Image Credit: Alberto E. Rodriguez/Getty Images Director ( The Wild Robot , Lilo & Stitch ) Sanders has helped shape mainstream animation for four decades, from story work on Disney classics including Beauty and the Beast and Aladdin to writing and directing Lilo & Stitch and How to Train Your Dragon . A four-time Oscar nominee, Sanders has shown that big-studio animation can combine commercial appeal with adventurous design and deeply emotional storytelling. Brad Schiff Image Credit: Courtesy of Laika Head of Animation, Laika Schiff oversees Laika’s stop-motion pipeline, the one responsible for Coraline , ParaNorman and the eagerly anticipated fantasy epic Wildwood . His work, pairing painstaking practical craftsmanship with newer tools like 3D-printed facial rigs, keeps Laika’s tactile, handmade identity intact even as the studio pushes into hybrid CGI territory. Matt Selman Image Credit: © Frank Micelotta/FOX Showrunner ( The Simpsons ) Seven-time Emmy winner Selman came up writing for Seinfeld before landing at the show he now runs day-to-day, charged with keeping its satirical edge and protecting its legacy. “You don’t want to be the person who ruins The Simpsons ,” he notes. Four decades in, he still sounds like a fan: “I’m so very, very, very proud that the writers of this 40-year-old show are still whipping up weird, funny, deep, surprising stories that are worthy of these iconic characters.” Domee Shi Image Credit: Deborah Coleman / Pixar Director ( Turning Red , Elio ) Shi has risen through the Pixar ranks, starting as a story intern, working on Inside Out , Incredibles 2 and Toy Story 4 , before writing and directing the Oscar-winning short Bao in 2019. Shi is now a Pixar vp creative, involved in key creative decisions across the studio. Makoto Shinkai Image Credit: Courtesy of Suzume Film Partners Director ( Your Name. , Suzume ) Shinkai has turned hyper-detailed backgrounds and aching romantic longing into box office gold, with Your Name. and Suzume both breaking records in Japan and helping spark a broader global anime moment. His meticulous, digitally driven visual style and commercial success won over Crunchyroll, which has picked up worldwide rights outside Asia and India to his next, unnamed feature. Nishimoto Shu President, Aniplex Nishimoto oversees an anime giant whose portfolio includes major franchises such as Demon Slayer , Fate and Sword Art Online , alongside games, theatrical distribution, licensing, merchandise and live events. Under Nishimoto, Aniplex is putting greater emphasis on international markets, working with Crunchyroll on global distribution. Andrew Stanton Image Credit: Deborah Coleman / Pixar Director ( WALL-E , Finding Nemo , Toy Story 5 ) A four-time Oscar winner, Stanton has spent more than three decades at Pixar as a writer, director and creative force behind some of the studio’s most influential films. After his triumphant animated return with Toy Story 5 , Stanton has said he wants to shift his focus to live action, but will keep a foot in Pixar, if only to help protect up-and-coming talents, like Daniel Chong, whose debut, Hoppers , Stanton helped defend against studio skeptics. Barbara Stephen Image Credit: Babara Stephen CEO, Flying Bark Stephen has helped transform Flying Bark Productions from an Australian children’s animation company into an international production powerhouse, combining original productions with animation services for global partners including Disney, Marvel, Netflix, Paramount and Nickelodeon. On AI, she takes a pragmatic view. “To me, the role of all emerging technologies is as a tool in service of the craft, to find real efficiencies in the pipeline, free up our crew to focus on higher-value work and facilitate more original storytelling,” she says. Tara Strong Image Credit: Tara Strong Voice Actor ( The Powerpuff Girls , Teen Titans Go! , Samurai Jack ) Strong is animation’s woman of a thousand voices, a prolific performer who has helped define the sound of multiple generations of animated characters, from Bubbles of The Powerpuff Girls and Twilight Sparkle in My Little Pony , to Batgirl, Raven and Harley Quinn in the DC animated universe. Toshio Suzuki Image Credit: Walt Disney/Courtesy Everett Collection Chairman, Studio Ghibli Suzuki has spent his tenure as Studio Ghibli’s chairman protecting the studio’s handcrafted legacy while still finding room to grow — expanding into digital distribution and international collaboration without diluting what made classics like Spirited Away , Princess Mononoke and Howl’s Moving Castle work in the first place. Genndy Tartakovsky Image Credit: Genndy Tartakovsky Director & Creator ( Hotel Transylvania , Samurai Jack ) Tartakovsky created Samurai Jack and the Hotel Transylvania franchise on the strength of a kinetic visual style and sharp comedic instincts that have carried through decades of work, including Dexter’s Laboratory and Primal . He’s now developing an animated Conan the Barbarian series for Prime Video, as executive producer and showrunner, that promises to bring the legendary swordsman into a fresh, action-driven format. Ami Thompson Image Credit: Courtesy of Disney Art Director ( KPop Demon Hunters , Raya and the Last Dragon ) As an art director, Thompson’s distinctive strength is her ability to combine characters and visual influences from very different worlds into a unified, graphic identity, whether that’s bringing together Disney princesses from multiple eras into a contemporary 3D aesthetic on Ralph Breaks the Internet or her bold mashup of K-pop glamour, anime-influenced character design and Korean mythology and shamanism on KPop Demon Hunters . Jae-myung Yoo CEO, Studio Mir Yoo has built Studio Mir into one of Korea’s most prominent animation studios for international productions, working on Nickelodeon’s The Legend of Korra and Voltron: Legendary Defender for DreamWorks and Netflix and on Netflix’s The Witcher animated spinoffs. He has used Mir’s blend of 2D animation craft and CGI production to move the studio from an overseas production partner toward a creator and production company in its own right. Fumio Yoshimura Image Credit: Netflix President & CEO, Toei Co. Yoshimura has led Toei Co., the parent company of Toei Animation, as president and CEO since 2023, bringing a background in content, media and international business to the company behind some of Japan’s most enduring entertainment franchises. His remit extends beyond animation to Toei’s film, television and live-entertainment operations, while Toei Animation remains the engine behind global properties including One Piece , Dragon Ball and Sailor Moon . Yang Yu Image Credit: Courtesy of A24 Director ( Ne Zha 2 ) Better known as Jiaozi, Yang directed Ne Zha 2 , the Chinese animated sequel that became a global box office phenomenon in 2025, earning $2.27 billion at the box office to become the most successful animated movie in history. (Disney’s Zootopia 2 , Hollywood’s top earner, is a distant second at $1.87 billion.) Unlike Japanese anime, Chinese animation hasn’t yet made the leap to mainstream success in the West, but with these numbers, it’s not clear why it needs to. Gints Zilbalodis Image Credit: Gints Zilbalodis Director ( Flow ) Zilbalodis turned an intimate, dialogue-free survival story into one of animation’s most unlikely recent breakthroughs with Flow , his independently produced feature about a cat navigating a world submerged by a catastrophic flood. Made mainly in Latvia on Blender, a free and open-source 3D graphics software, Flow won the 2025 best animated feature Oscar, becoming the first independent film to take the prize (as well as the first-ever Latvian Oscar). Zilbalodis is already chasing that same spirit of risk on his follow-up. “I’ve been working on my new film Limbo ,” he says. “With my team, we have been challenging ourselves to try some crazy ideas and to do things in very unconventional ways, which have been scary, but also very rewarding.” This story appeared in the Oct. 7 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

title: Reinaldo Marcus Green Launches Film Fellowship At His Alma Mater NYU Tisch School Of The Arts, Reveals Inaugural Class
full_text: Skip to main content By Patrick Hipes Patrick Hipes Executive Managing Editor More Stories By Patrick Reinaldo Marcus Green Launches Film Fellowship At His Alma Mater NYU Tisch School Of The Arts, Reveals Inaugural Class ‘Being Heumann’ Trailer: First Extended Look At Siân Heder’s ‘CODA’ Follow-Up Sony’s Screen Gems Sets YouTube Exec Fede Goldenberg To Top Genre Label; Ashley Brucks Segues To Producer Role View All October 13, 2026 8:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Reinaldo Marcus Green Arturo Holmes/Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: King Richard and Bob Marley: One Love director Reinaldo Marcus Green has launched Office Hours, a new filmmaker fellowship at his alma mater the NYU Tisch School of the Arts. The fellowship has also selected its inaugural class of five filmmakers who are all recent alums or current students in the graduate film program. The fellowship, created to provide emerging filmmakers with access, mentorship and candid conversation about the creative and professional realities of building a career in film, will bring its fellows together with Green for a series of intimate sessions throughout the academic year on topics like developing a voice, choosing material, working with actors and collaborators, navigating representation and relationships, dealing with setbacks, and building a sustainable career. Related Stories News David Oyelowo & Viola Prettejohn To Star In ‘The Girl With The Dragon Tattoo’ TV Series For Sky News ‘King Richard’ Director Reinaldo Marcus Green To Helm Roberto Clemente Biopic For Teton Ridge This year’s cohort — Alex Jiang, Maissa Lihedheb, Skyla Page, Andre Shen and Taylor Sanghyun Lee — were selected by a committee of filmmakers including Kasi Lemmons, John Tintori, Chiara Bernasconi and Mia Cioffi Henry. (See details about the inaugural class below.) Watch on Deadline “When I was coming out of NYU, what I needed as much as anything was access — someone I could call, ask the questions I didn’t know how to ask, and have an honest conversation about what this career actually looks like,” Green said. He added: “Office Hours is my attempt to create that space for the next generation of filmmakers. These five filmmakers already have extraordinary voices. My job isn’t to tell them what kind of filmmakers to become. It’s to listen, challenge them, share what I’ve learned, and hopefully help them get where they’re trying to go.” Green directed 2021’s King Richard , the story of the rise of tennis’ Venus and Serena Williams and their father-coach. The pic scored six Oscar nominations including Best Picture, and earned star Will Smith the Best Actor Oscar. He follow that up co-writing and directing 2024’s Bob Marley: One Love . His credits also include the TV series We Own This City and Netflix’s Top Boy . His debut feature, Monsters and Men starring John David Washington, Anthony Ramos and Kelvin Harrison Jr., world premiered at the 2018 Sundance Film Festival. He’s now working on Sky’s TV adaptation The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo , on which he directs and executive produces. “Having this kind of guidance from an established filmmaker like Rei is an incredible opportunity for our students and recent alumni as they navigate their first steps in the industry,” says Andrew Okpeaha MacLean, chair of the Tisch Department of Graduate Film. Below are more details on this year’s fellows, per Office Hours: ALEX JIANG Alex Jiang is a Hong Kong-born, New York-based filmmaker exploring bodily autonomy and queer desire through folklore and a feminist, Asian diasporic lens. A USC BFA graduate and NYU Tisch MFA candidate, her shorts have screened at Palm Springs ShortFest, Los Angeles Asian Pacific Film Festival and Taiwan International Queer Film Festival. She participated in the Shanghai International Film Festival Director’s Lab and Diverso Fellowship and is a member of the 2026 Film at Lincoln Center Artists Academy. As a producer, she is developing Circle, one of 12 projects selected for the 15th Biennale College Cinema. MAISSA LIHEDHEB Maissa Lihedheb is a German-Tunisian filmmaker whose work explores identity, performance and the contradictions of belonging through dark humor and emotionally charged storytelling. Her films have screened at Tribeca, BFI London, Palm Springs ShortFest and El Gouna. Her work has been featured by Vogue Arabia, Rolling Stone MENA, ARTE and Highsnobiety. A two-time Ang Lee Scholar, Spike Lee Grant recipient and Princess Grace honoree, she completed her MFA at NYU Tisch Graduate Film and is currently developing the feature films Wedding and a Funeral, Carapace and The Good One. SKYLA PAGE Skyla Page is a writer, director and cinematographer from Chicago, now based in Brooklyn. She earned her MFA from NYU Tisch Graduate Film. As a cinematographer, she received the Nestor Almendros Craft Award for Cinematography, and her work has screened at the First Run and Atlanta Film Festivals. She received the Spike Lee Production Fund for her upcoming short Rise & Fly and is currently developing her debut narrative feature, Full Bloom. ANDRE SHEN Andre Shen is a Shanghainese writer-director and graphic designer based in New York. His work explores queer longing and emotional exposure through pop culture, orbiting an obsession with performance across gender, theater and sex. His films have screened at BFI Flare, MiXMilano and FiveFilmsForFreedom in partnership with the British Council. His upcoming short Hit It Out of the Park follows a rising pop star and his self-proclaimed creative director as their music video shoot unravels. He is currently preparing his feature. TAYLOR SANGHYUN LEE Born and raised in California, Taylor Sanghyun Lee is a New York-based filmmaker whose work spans writing, directing and cinematography. His directorial debut feature, ROUNDS, was selected for the 2026 Sundance Directors & Screenwriters Lab, the 2026 NYU Purple List and the 2025 TIFF & CJ K-Story Fund. He earned his MFA in Directing from NYU Tisch Graduate Film, where he received the Ang Lee Scholarship. His upcoming short Parkside East won the 2026 DGA Student Spotlight Award and was a semifinalist for the 2026 Student Academy Awards. title: Discovery+ Raises Prices In One Of Skydance’s First Streaming Moves After Merger Close
full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Discovery+ Raises Prices In One Of Skydance’s First Streaming Moves After Merger Close Prime Video Adds Golf’s Revived Skins Game To 15-Hour Live Sports Blitz On Black Friday Sony Ups Tim Erickson To CEO Of Peanuts Worldwide, Appoints Ken Ohtake As Chairman View All October 13, 2026 8:28am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Discovery's Shark Week programming is featured on streaming service Discovery+ Courtesy As it begins its second week as a bulked-up public company, Skydance has raised prices of stand-alone streaming service Discovery+ . The base-level, ad-supported tier now costs $6.99 a month, up $1, and the “ad-light” higher tier is $11.99, a $2 increase. Skydance was formed from the merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery , which officially closed last week. The new company is saddled with nearly $80 billion in debt and has pledged to whittle it down along with delivering $6 billion in cost savings. Along with back-end efficiencies, real estate sales and layoffs, higher streaming rates are expected, in keeping with inflation across the media sector of late. Related Stories News 'M+/HBO Originals': Movistar Plus & Skydance Extend Partnership News Who Is In Charge At Skydance International - For Now At Least Discovery+, which features programming from a range of cable networks, has remained a stand-alone since its launch in 2021. It initially was priced at $4.99 for the base tier and $6.99 for the plan with fewer ads, offering 50,000 hours of programming from networks like TLC, Discovery, HGTV and the Food Network. Watch on Deadline After former parent Discovery Communications merged with WarnerMedia in 2022, the new parent looked at combining Discovery+ with HBO Max and went so far as to rebrand the latter as Max to reflect a broader content offering. Audiences and partners balked at the mixture of upmarket HBO fare with lifestyle and unscripted fare, and the corporate bosses preserved Discovery+ as a lower-priced option for consumers. In part because the company does not commission originals for Discovery+, it has been profitable for most of its existence. HBO Max announced a round of price hikes last fall, with the basic ad-tier rising $1 to $10.99 a month and the popular Standard plan climbing to $18.49. title: Amanda Seyfried Says She Won’t Do Projects With Sex Scenes: “I’m Uncomfortable With It”

I’m uncomfortable with it. I’m not into it right now.” Seyfried, who has in the past done racy projects like Jennifer’s Body and Lovelace , says she’s in a different place in her life. “I have kids now who are paying attention to what I do,” she told interviewer Alec Baldwin during the conversation. title: Ben Affleck Says ‘Justice League’ Was A “Low Point” In His Career
full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Ego Nwodim Reacts To Shane Gillis’ Controversial ‘SNL’ Joke: “Whore Reporting For Duty” Robert Pattinson Shares Update On ‘The Batman Part II’: “We Are Going To Figure It All Out” ‘Coven Academy’s Devon Sawa Struggled With Being Recognized For ‘Casper’ Years After Starring In Role: “I Gotta Embrace It” View All October 12, 2026 4:11pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ben Affleck filming 'Justice League' Clay Enos / Warner Bros. Pictures Ben Affleck is getting real about the “low point” of his career, pinpointing it to the time he was filming Justice League . In a new interview, the actor opened up about the reshoots and how Warner Bros . handled the whole situation. “The truth is, the experience of Justice League was so, so negative for lots of different reasons,” Affleck said on the Happy Sad Confused podcast. “Some of which having to do with where I was personally, some of which having to do with the tragedy that happened during the time, and also the fact that I really saw how not to make a movie like that when the studio is at odds with the filmmaker. title: ‘Half’ Review: Hip-Hop Beats & Brutal Beatings In Samjad’s Fast, Fun, Super-Violent Indian Vampire Horror Movie – Sitges Film Festival
full_text: Skip to main content By Damon Wise Damon Wise Film Editor, Awards yo_damo More Stories By Damon ‘Half’ Review: Hip-Hop Beats & Brutal Beatings In Samjad’s Fast, Fun, Super-Violent Indian Vampire Horror Movie – Sitges Film Festival Marie-Clémentine Dusabejambo On Directing Rwanda’s Oscar Submission ‘Ben’Imana’: “We Need To Understand What Happened” – Contenders London ‘Wildwood’ Director Travis Knight On Laika’s Stop-Motion Fantasy Epic: “It Took Us 16 Years To Make This Movie” – Contenders London View All October 12, 2026 4:32pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Half’ TIFF Two halves make a satisfying whole in this lean, mean action-horror, in which twin vampires stalk a scorching-hot Madras Max: Fury Road dystopia in the none-too-distant future. The 1996 Robert Rodriguez/Quentin Tarantino collaboration From Dusk Till Dawn springs immediately to mind, but, compared to that, director Samjad sinks his teeth into the meat of his movie in next to no time. Scored with an urgent techno-bhangra beat by Midhun Mukundan, the result is a violent revenge thriller that has been lapped up on the genre circuit since it premiered in the Midnight Madness strand at TIFF this year. Related Stories News Top 50 Halloween Movies Photo Gallery: Creepy Classics From ‘Psycho,’ ‘The Shining’ To ‘Obsession’ & ‘Get Out’ News Horror Movies’ Next Wave: What’s Coming In 2026, From Auteur Nightmares To Indie Breakouts The film starts with the minimum of backstory, which is at odds not only with the norms of Indian cinema but also the press book, which suggests that a whole lot of exposition about the genesis of the story’s two siblings has been cut. This might be for the better; our introduction to Ethan and Ivy (Ranjith Sajeev and Aiswarya Raj) is brief but suitably ominous. “Born of mortal dust and vampire blood, the twins walk in darkness,” a title card tells us, before we’re shown a brief flashback to their seemingly idyllic childhood where the two fight like cat and dog (“Raising you two will be the end of me,” says their mother). Cut to the present, where the two are taking a road trip to the much busier Mumbai district of Pai Nagar in shades that not only protect them from the sun but, conveniently, make them also look very, very cool. As they make their way, we cut to a family of four making the same trip across the desert, passing Babu’s Puncture Shop, whose owner makes a phone call. Soon the family is being tailed by a couple on a scooter, carrying what appears to be a baby and yelling, “Sir! Sir! Oil leak!” The father pulls over, and the car is immediately swarmed over by bandits, who brutally kill him — plus his wife and two kids — with no mercy. Watch on Deadline The aftermath of the crime is cleaned up with ruthless efficiency, the gang hauling off the car, stripping it for parts and burning the bodies of the victims, a process that threatens to rinse and repeat when Ethan and Ivy follow almost immediately in the same slipway. The murder of the family is graphic enough, but what happens to Ethan and Ivy is far more perverse, especially when Ivy’s apparently dead body is defiled by one of the feral desert gang members. Samjad keeps the twins’ superpowers under wraps for an agonizingly long time, until the sun goes down and their bodies are able to regenerate. The wait is worth it; when Ethan and Ivy finally take their revenge on this criminal outfit — one by one, piece by piece — it’s with a satisfying sense of bone-cracking justice, orchestrated like S. S. Rajamouli’s 2022 breakout hit RRR at 200mph. The genius of Samjad’s conceit, however, is that, for all their superhuman abilities, the twins are vulnerable — not only is sunlight their only weakness, Ivy also is deaf and non-verbal, which adds a real sense of threat towards the end, when things look very bleak indeed. Part of this is down to Samjad’s fantastic sense of world-building; like Peter Weir’s 1974 black comedy The Cars That Ate Paris , Half is a sardonic comment on the sleazy eco-system of crime: Babu’s Puncture Shop is just one layer in a pyramid that goes surprisingly high and eclipses even the bumbling, paid-off police force, which willfully sees no evil and nervously treats each investigation as “extra paperwork.” There’s also a twitchy paranoia at play, since Ethan and Ivy, as outsiders, inevitably spark a turf war as various warring factions try to figure out who is killing their men. There aren’t too many directors that can sustain this level of inventive carnage — even Takashi Miike has yet to show a man choking to death on the stump of his own severed hand — but Samjad directs the action with clarity and skill, helped immeasurably by Very Tri Yulisman’s incredible fight choreography. A puzzling coda means the film ends later than it probably should, but Samjad already has established his impressive cult bona fides: If you only see one gory Malayalam neo-noir spaghetti western vampire beat-’em-up in your life, make it this one. title: suspending the White House TV pool
full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Antitrust Experts Doubt Donald Trump’s DOJ Has A Case In Going After Networks For Suspending White House TV Pool ABC Tells Judge That FCC Showed “Retaliatory Motive” By Ordering Early License Review Despite “Less Intrusive” Options Judge Orders Trump Administration To Stop Running Taxpayer Funded Ads That Promote POTUS View All September 21, 2026 7:16am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Donald Trump Getty UPDATED: When Donald Trump travels to New York on Monday, there will be no primary TV pool, after major networks declined to replace CNN in the regular rotation after it was banned from White House and other coverage of the president. CNN was scheduled to serve as the pool network, but the White House released a schedule late Sunday showing that was no longer the case. On Friday, Trump announced a ban on CNN, Politico and MS NOW from White House access because of their negative coverage of him. The five major networks in the pool — CNN, Fox News , ABC, NBC and CBS — indicated that there would be no such TV coverage as long as the restrictions remain in place. Related Stories News Judge Orders Trump Administration To Stop Running Taxpayer Funded Ads That Promote POTUS News DOJ Launches Investigation Of Networks For Suspending TV Pool Amid Trump's Ban On CNN “This is to advise that, effective today, the TV pool will not be covering events designated as pool coverage of the president,” read a message from Fox News Washington bureau chief Bryan Boughton, who is currently chairing the pool. “This follows the White House’s position preventing CNN from fulfilling its assigned pool duties. There will be no replacement pool put in place.” Watch on Deadline He added, “All other pool coverage will continue as normal, including Congress, VIPs, and selected events in Washington and around this country. We will provide further updates as this situation develops.” The pool provides coverage guidance on a day-to-day basis, so it was not immediately clear how long the suspension will last. But it is taking place during an eventful week: Trump is addressing the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday. Later in the week, he will host Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, including for a state dinner. In a statement, the five networks in the TV pool stated, “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.” The network pool distributes video and audio to other outlets, a system designed to rotate responsibilities and costs while gaining access where space is limited. Earlier today, CNN, Politico and MS NOW announced that they were filing a lawsuit against Trump and other members of the administration, claiming First Amendment retaliation and violation of due process. The lawsuit seeks a restoration of journalists’ access and credentials. Print, photo and radio pool coverage is scheduled to continue, as well as secondary TV poolers. After the networks announced that there would be no pool, the White House directed users to live stream updates on its app, which it labeled as “Trump TV.” The lack of a TV pool was evident at midday on Monday, when the networks skipped coverage of a ribbon cutting ceremony on the South Lawn for the new White House helipad. Other outlets showed their support for CNN. The Washington Post said it was joining a “collective effort with photographers in other newsrooms covering the White House in a show of support of the banned outlets.” The Post said that it would not publish any photos of presidential events until midnight ET. PBS said that it would not publish video or still images provided by the administration. Per The New York Times, NPR told staffers that it wouldn’t use audio from White House events until further notice. title: Antitrust Experts Doubt Donald Trump’s DOJ Has A Case In Going After Networks For Suspending White House TV Pool
full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted New White House Press Secretary Debuts With A Very Short Briefing, Some Breaking News And Lots Of Praise For Donald Trump ABC Tells Judge That FCC Showed “Retaliatory Motive” By Ordering Early License Review Despite “Less Intrusive” Options Judge Orders Trump Administration To Stop Running Taxpayer Funded Ads That Promote POTUS View All October 12, 2026 5:20pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source The U.S. Department of Justice building in Washington, D.C. Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images News that the Justice Department is investigating five major networks for suspending the White House TV pool last month was met with outcry that it was another example of Trump administration retaliation against the media . Alarming as it may be to First Amendment groups, among antitrust experts, there are doubts that the DOJ would have much of a case. Related Stories News White House Video Coverage Returns As Networks Resume TV Pool; CNN Says It’s Being Allowed Back In After Judge Sidelines Trump Ban News CNN, MS NOW And Politico Sue Donald Trump Over His White House Ban Section 1 of the Sherman Antitrust Act restricts competitors that restrain competition. In this case, the five networks that make up the TV pool — CNN , Fox News , ABC News , CBS News and NBC News — last month withheld their participation to protest the White House’s exclusion of CNN . For about four days, that meant fewer video images and other coverage of Trump that week, including the ceremonies surrounding the visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping. William Kovacic, global competition professor of law and policy at George Washington University, said, “I think you have to take any lawsuit from the Department of Justice seriously.” Watch on Deadline But he said an antitrust claim against the networks likely would have a “very remote prospect of success.” At issue is “what is the predominant character of the behavior: Is it a commercial interest or is it designed to achieve some form of First Amendment expression?” “To me, if there is a commercial aim to this, it is well hidden,” said Kovacic, a former chairman of the Federal Trade Commission. Diana Moss, vice president and director of competition policy at the Progressive Policy Institute, said via email, “Group boycotts are illegal when they stifle competition, such as forcing a competitor(s) out of the market.” She added, “Presumably, the arrangement among the five networks is designed to increase coordination and efficiency in the distribution of news footage. There is no anti-competitive intent or effect. The networks were responding in solidarity to repression of a free press (1st Amendment).” Court Precedence The lines between commercial conduct and protected First Amendment activity can be blurred, but courts have sided with boycotting parties even then. Sam Weinstein, professor at Cardozo School of Law and former attorney in the DOJ’s Antitrust Division, said that “typically a non commercial boycott is protected by the First Amendment.” “It would seem to be a non starter,” he said. He cited the Supreme Court’s 1982 decision in NAACP vs. Claiborne Hardware Co., involving an organized 1960s-era boycott of white-owned businesses in Mississippi. The justices held that the state could not hold the protesters liable for damages when they engage in lawful activity protected by the First Amendment. Weinstein also referred to another Supreme Court case, FTC vs. Superior Court Trial Lawyers, when the justices ruled that a boycott by court-appointed lawyers for indigent defendants violated antitrust law, as its purpose was to to gain increased compensation. The majority compared it to horizontal price fixing. The latter case, Weinstein said, is different from what happened with the TV pool. Prices and compensation were not at issue. It’s still unclear whether the networks will comply with the DOJ investigative request, but the networks already made it clear that they were jointly suspending participation in the pool, releasing a statement that “no administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.” “The real question is a question of law, not a question of fact,” Weinstein said. In a statement, a spokesperson for the DOJ said over the weekend, “Members of the television press pool have boycotted covering White House events. Group boycotts among commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act. The Antitrust Division is simply investigating to determine whether these news organizations have violated the antitrust laws.” “An End Run Around” Democrats already have accused the Trump administration of politicizing the Antitrust Division, violating the norms that have separated the White House from the DOJ since the Nixon era. The investigation of the networks is likely to add another example to their arguments. Bob Corn-Revere, chief counsel for the Foundation for Individual Rights and Expression, said via email, “Threatening an antitrust investigation is just another example of this Administration misusing regulatory authority to punish the media for doing something the President dislikes. Political boycotts are part of a longstanding American tradition and are protected under First Amendment law.” He added, “Whether the government’s excuses are dressed up as ‘national security’ or antitrust law, this is another attempt by the Administration trying to make an end run around the First Amendment to control news coverage.” White House Press Secretary’s Debut: Very Short, Some News, Much Trump Praise The YouTube Age: Content Creators Making Waves In Europe Toon Comedy ‘Merrick & Treves’ From ‘Archer’ Team Lands Two-Season HBO Order Cranston & Other ‘Breaking Bad’ Alums Mourn Actor Who Played Walt Jr. Read More About: 2 Comments
